title: Finish moving the estate off the node20 Actions runtime: the repositories and composite actions the first sweep missed.
description: The 2026-09-19 sweep was reported complete and was not. It inventoried 51 repos; there are 117 active ones across jeremylongshore and the intent-solutions-io org, and 29 affected repos were never scanned. It also never looked inside composite actions: codecov-action v5 runs github-script v7 (node20) on every run, upload-pages-artifact v3/v4 wrap upload-artifact v4. Second pass 2026-09-20: 41 repos, 55 workflow files, 40 PRs on branch ci/node20-second-pass. Also found and fixed: release.yml unloadable in waygate-mcp and diagnosticpro-schema-sql (templated column-0 heredoc), intent-blue-gold hash manifest stale on its default branch (issue #130). intent-os needs no change (the node20 step inside open-code-review only runs with upload_artifacts true).
close_reason: Second node20 pass done 2026-09-20. 41 repos / 55 workflow files found by a full inventory of all 117 active repos in both accounts, resolving composite actions one level down. 40 PRs on ci/node20-second-pass: 39 merged (incl. intent-eval-core #95 and marketplace #1561: codecov-action v5 runs github-script v7 node20 on every run, moved to v6). Hash-pinned repos re-pinned with their own harness and the manifest diff classified (only edited files' pins moved). Re-scan after merges: 121 refs, 2 remaining, both known: intent-longbox-archive #113 left open because its required dependency audit already fails on main (2 medium advisories, not mine to bypass), and intent-os open-code-review whose inner node20 upload step only runs with upload_artifacts true (set false; upstream latest still has it). Side finds fixed: release.yml unloadable in waygate-mcp and diagnosticpro-schema-sql; filed intent-blue-gold#130 (stale hash manifest, CI never runs verify).

title: Sweep the rest of the estate off the node20 GitHub Actions runtime before 2026-09-23
description: GitHub removes the node20 Actions runtime on 2026-09-23. Any job using an action whose action.yml declares 'using: node20' will fail to start. The six Intent Eval Platform repos were swept and verified clean on 2026-09-19 (closed bead under the eval-evolution epic). A read-only grep of LOCAL checkouts (possibly stale, not fetched) found node20-era pins in many other repos. Production or client relevant: hustle (22 pins, deploys prod), claude-code-plugins (36, bespoke CI: study before touching, per standing feedback), braves (9, prod deploy), intent-os (8, self-hosted runner: also confirm the runner version itself supports node24), diagnostic-pro (15), nixtla (142, client repo), bobs-big-brain-compiler (15), bobs-big-brain-plugin (10), iams/bobs-brain and iam-bob-adk (80 each), perception (31), intentvision (27), stci (24), executive-intent (22), intent-blueprint-docs (20), ai-devops-intent-solutions (20), twenty-mcp (6), omarchy-typing-adventure (7). Ignore contributing-clanker/* (upstream forks) and archived repos. Method that worked: inventory every 'uses: owner/repo[/sub]@ref', read 'using:' from that action's own action.yml at the pinned ref, bump to the lowest node24 major. Lowest node24 majors: checkout 5, setup-node 5, upload-artifact 6, download-artifact 7, setup-python 6, cache 5, github-script 8, codeql-action 4, pnpm/action-setup 5, markdownlint-cli2-action 23. Expect two side effects: repos that hash-pin workflows need audit-harness init plus a line-by-line check of the .harness-hash diff, and markdownlint-cli2-action 23 adds MD060 (estate convention is to disable it because it fights Prettier). Full notes: Claude memory reference-github-actions-node20-removal. Prioritize repos that deploy to the VPS; each owning session should do its own repo.
notes: 2026-09-19 sweep executed on owner instruction. Scope: 51 owned, non-archived, non-fork repos with node20/16/12 action pins (5 forks and 2 archived repos skipped per standing rules). Method: fresh shallow clones (no local working tree touched), every uses: ref inventoried (111 distinct), runtime read from each action's own action.yml at the pinned ref, only node20/16/12 refs rewritten, SHA pins kept as SHA pins, lowest node24 major for third-party actions. 50 PRs opened, 47 MERGED. Re-inventory straight from GitHub default branches afterwards: 47 of 51 repos have zero non-node24 actions. Production deploys that ran THROUGH the bumped actions and succeeded, with live 200/healthy checks: braves-booth (scorecardecho.com), comehomealabama, jeremylongshore.com, intent-solutions-landing (intentsolutions.io), DiagnosticPro, hustle (hustlestats.io /api/health healthy). Prerequisite: jeremylongshore/minimax-code-review fork was node20 and SHA-pinned in 16 repos; fork main migrated via PR #2 (cherry-pick of upstream afc68845), and consumers re-pinned to 2f8eefa on branch pinned/d1314b9-node24 = exactly the trusted d1314b9 plus the one runtime line, deliberately excluding bcaa651's endpoint/model default change. KEEP THAT BRANCH. Regressions caused by the bump and fixed in-PR: setup-go v6 exports GOTOOLCHAIN=local (iam-bob-eino govulncheck needs step-level GOTOOLCHAIN=auto; gastown-viewer-intent pinned go 1.22 against go.mod 1.24, now go-version-file); golangci-lint-action has no node24 release below v9 which forces golangci-lint v2 and 18 new findings in gastown, so v1.64.8 is now installed directly. iam-local-rag: harness check was already failing on untouched main because CI installs intent-audit-harness unpinned and 1.4.0 tracks more files; re-pinned as a separate commit after proving 5 files newly tracked, 0 dropped, 0 already-pinned hashes changed. 13 PRs merged with red checks after job-level proof each failure also fails on the default branch (or is dead GCP Workload Identity auth, or MCP SDK drift in plugins-nixtla, or an unpinned RuboCop cop); each has an audit comment. OPEN: guidewire-mcp-for-claude #153 and intent-vision #11 are green but need an approving review (no admin override used). tons-of-skills-marketplace #1554 NOT merged: its cold cache exposed that better-sqlite3 12.11.1 ships no Node 20 (ABI 115) binary, so Node 20 jobs only pass on main via pnpm's side-effects cache and will break on the next lockfile change regardless; documented on the PR with three options, decision left to that repo. Unfixable by version bump: actions/create-release (node12, archived) in marketplace cli-publish.yml and codecov/test-results-action@v1 in bobs-big-brain-compiler. Three workflow files already had invalid YAML before this sweep: iam-git-with-intent deploy.yml, intent-solutions-landing astro-site release.yml, prompts-intent-solutions release.yml. Three plugin-shipped workflow files inside marketplace plugins/** still reference node20 actions (product content, deliberately untouched).
close_reason: Complete 2026-09-19. All 50 PRs merged across 51 owned, non-archived, non-fork repos (guidewire-mcp-for-claude #153 and intent-vision #11 admin-merged on owner instruction while green; tons-of-skills-marketplace #1554 merged with 50 of 50 checks green after moving its CI baseline to Node 22 and regenerating a drifted scorecard). Re-inventory straight from GitHub default branches: zero node20/16/12 actions remain anywhere except two with no node24 release upstream (actions/create-release in the marketplace cli-publish.yml, codecov/test-results-action in bobs-big-brain-compiler), both tracked. Production deploys ran green through the bumped actions: braves-booth, comehomealabama, jeremylongshore.com, intent-solutions-landing, DiagnosticPro, hustle, intent-os, and tonsofskills.com (its first successful deploy since 2026-08-26, after fixing an unrelated Tailscale OIDC subject mismatch and a root-privilege bug in the VPS deploy script). Everything the sweep exposed but did not cause is tracked under the CI-debt epic with one GitHub issue per affected repo (21 issues). Forks and archived repos were skipped by rule and have their own bead.

title: Implement fail-closed dependency scanning in audit-harness

Preserve the zero-runtime-dependency and read-only harness boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Lockfile detection and applicability are deterministic; OSV invocation is wired and version/evidence metadata is emitted; required mode fails closed for scanner absence/crash; findings are classified by production versus development exposure under a documented policy; no applicable dependency manifests yields NOT_APPLICABLE; golden tests cover all failure and success paths; registry/docs/CLI/CI/release behavior remain synchronized; full repository gates pass.

title: Make dependency and baseline security gates universally fail-closed and evidenced
description: The audit harness models OSV and related security gates, but dependency scanning is advisory, tool absence can silently degrade to indeterminate, and CI/release/template consumers do not prove that required scans ran. Audit the central harness for analogous enforcement gaps, implement the critical fail-closed contracts centrally, release them, and propagate the versioned contract through Omarchy and other applicable consumers without duplicating workflow logic.
acceptance_criteria: A repository with a supported dependency lockfile runs a deterministic vulnerability scan and emits machine-readable evidence; missing/crashed required scanners fail closed in CI and release contexts; repositories with no applicable dependencies emit justified NOT_APPLICABLE; production and development exposure are distinguished by documented policy; the harness self-tests happy/finding/missing-tool/crash/no-dependency paths; other obvious universal security-control gaps are audited and either fixed or tracked with evidence; a reviewed release is published before consumer propagation; Omarchy and applicable estate consumers pin and execute the released contract; all Beads/GitHub/Plane mirrors and validation receipts are synchronized.

title: Alert when a spec baseline stays stale, not when an upstream page changes
description: c875cf1 (2026-06-24) stopped byte-hash drift from alerting; only semantic drift (FF#2) or a liveness trip does. That change was CORRECT and must not be reverted - byte-hash on a docs page fires on typo fixes and nav reshuffles, and 13 such issues had accumulated with zero semantic drift behind them. The problem is composition: FF#2, the only remaining alerting path, is structurally incapable of firing, so a gate meant to suppress noise now suppresses everything and 11 drifted sources have gone unreported since mid-June. The signal is NOT missing - emit-snapshot-currency.py already emits a row carrying all 11 snapshot-drift reasons, advisory, alerting nowhere. Route it, do not invent a new detector. FIX: track per-surface consecutive-runs-drifted-without-baseline-advance in .state.json (which already carries fetch_error_streak / last_ok_utc), alert when the streak crosses a threshold, keep byte-hash detection and reporting exactly as today, route via Slack not a daily GitHub issue (issue-per-day produced the 13-issue pileup). HARD PREREQ: .state.json durability - it last persisted 2026-07-06 and live state lives in the evictable Actions cache, so a streak counter there resets to zero and never trips. Land this BEFORE the FF#2 repairs: it is the safety net that catches the next silent break, including a botched repair. GitHub #15.

title: Make FF#2 diff freshly captured upstream content instead of two frozen committed files
description: spec-projection-diff.py cmd_check() extracts from a committed snapshot on disk and diffs it against the committed projection.v1.json - both operands frozen, so it reports 'NO semantic drift (0 findings)' by construction and would keep doing so if every upstream page were rewritten. The local variable is literally named 'fresh' and is not. Snapshot header reads 'Fetched: 2026-05-28'. The offline property is DELIBERATE and good (Armstrong firewall: only a FETCH_OK snapshot reaches the differ) - the bug is that the gated stage meant to feed it fresh content is the one blocked by branch protection, so the firewall has become a wall around a frozen room. FIX: keep the differ network-free (it takes paths, not URLs); have the workflow capture fresh content via fetch-capture.py, gate on FETCH_OK as today, and pass THAT directory to --check, so the diff is fresh-capture-projection vs committed-projection. Necessary but NOT sufficient - must land with the wrong-vendor-tree fix or the differ stays blind. --self-test already proves the differ detects every drift class, so the logic is sound; the defect is entirely in what it is fed. GitHub #12.

validation only; audit-harness, j-rig, and intent-rollout-gate gate nothing there. Deterministic
baseline measured 2026-07-22 at audit-harness@1.3.0: 2,446 skillmd PASS / 10 ADVISORY / 0 FAIL,

epic); children #11-#16 and #18.

Related prior postmortem bead: bd_000-projects-n2k2 (2026-06-28). Its L1 fix (SPEC_DRIFT_PUSH_TOKEN)
genuinely worked 2026-06-29 to 2026-07-06 (daily bot heartbeats in git), then silently expired. As of

specs/snapshots/.sha/ have never been bot-advanced — last write was a human PR on 2026-06-11.

Decisions taken 2026-07-22: remediation is suggest-only (no bot write path, which also removes the
prompt-injection write surface and the auto-bump re-head collision); audit-harness conform goes
required immediately once its 10 advisories clear (deterministic, so doc 110's flap soak does not

THE RISK TO DESIGN AGAINST: do not bulk-refresh. Re-baselining six weeks of unexamined upstream into
authoring/v1 turns a detector failure into a contract rewrite. One surface at a time; human
field-level reconciliation before any kernel schema edit; --refresh never across all 16 in one pass;
each fold-in its own reviewable PR. Prefer under-folding to over-folding.

title: Write Evidence Bundle predicate compatibility policy BEFORE first prod-Rekor anchor
description:
Per IEP thinker-panel review (Kleppmann finding #4, Fowler most-costly-to-recover-from, 2026-05-25). Rekor anchoring is a one-way door — once gate-result/v1 rows are signed into prod Rekor, the URI namespace is permanent forever. The compatibility policy MUST be written and ratified BEFORE iah-E06 pre-flight passes.

Policy MUST specify: (a) FORWARD rule (v1 consumer ignores unknown fields in v2 rows), (b) BACKWARD rule (v2 consumer reads v1 rows unmodified), (c) MIXING rule (bundles MAY contain rows of different versions; consumers process each row independently), (d) DEPRECATION rule (vN supported for at least 3 years after v(N+1)).

Landing place: intent-eval-lab/specs/evidence-bundle/COMPATIBILITY.md. Should be made an iec-E12 precondition.

This is a one-way door. Recovery cost = abandon v1 namespace and start over at v2 (forfeits first-mover-on-attested-evidence claim).

Fallback if not closed: Phases A+B ship as v0.1.0 milestone without Phase C.

title: Replace the wildcard Tailscale trust with per-repository trusts
description: An audit of all 18 Tailscale federated trusts on 2026-09-19 found one with subject repo:jeremylongshore/*:ref:refs/heads/main. It is how repos without their own trust (braves-booth, comehomealabama and others) deploy today, so do not delete it first: list which deploy workflows rely on it (their TS_AUDIENCE points at it), create a per-repo trust for each per intent-os ops/deploy/runbooks/onboard-a-repo.md, switch their two secrets, prove a deploy, then delete the wildcard. Note it cannot match repos that send GitHub's immutable OIDC subject. GitHub: intent-solutions-io/intent-os#630.
close_reason: Wildcard trust repo:jeremylongshore/*:ref:refs/heads/main DELETED 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200). It was worse than described: scope all and NO tags, so any repo under the account could mint a full-scope Tailscale API token from main. Sole dependent was braves-booth (117 repos swept for the TS secrets, 16 holders, 15 had their own trust). Created WIF braves-booth (tag:ci, subject read from GitHub), switched its two secrets through blind pipes, waited for that day's Braves game to go final and the booth poller to report running=false, then proved a production deploy: run 35538613522, Tailscale connect + deploy + smoke all success. Before deleting, confirmed all 16 holders set their secrets within seconds of their own trust's creation. After: 18 trusts, 0 wildcard, 0 untagged. Evidence + rollback definition: intent-os PR #640. Follow-up filed: narrow all trusts from scope all to auth_keys (intent-os#639).

title: Bound generic runner output and terminate descendant processes
description: Release-hardening follow-up discovered while integrating the generic runner in J-Rig #248 under htjt.15. packages/core/src/execution/executable-runner.ts accumulates stdout/stderr Buffer arrays without a byte ceiling and sends TERM/KILL only to the immediate child. A harness with inherited-pipe descendants can keep close pending beyond timeout, and excessive output can exhaust host memory. The current source example explicitly restricts this to trusted local code, not a sandbox. Keep hosted/untrusted use and package-release readiness unclaimed until bounded behavior is implemented and proved.
acceptance_criteria: Enforce documented output-size ceilings, bounded timeout completion and descendant cleanup on supported OSes; record an explicit runner infrastructure failure without a quality Grade; add deterministic oversized-output and inherited-pipe/grandchild regressions with cleanup; preserve successful stdout and sealed-run reuse. title: Validate the first international parent-market wedge

Add focused transport, runner, CLI, and regression tests.

title: Chain the beads git-sync hooks into husky in the compiler and registrar — core.hooksPath points at .husky/_ so the beads shims never fire
description:
DEFECT (found during the 2026-07-29 repo sweep, verified in both repos):

bobs-big-brain-compiler and bobs-big-brain-registrar both have a COMPLETE set of
beads hook shims at .beads/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,post-checkout,post-merge,
prepare-commit-msg} that correctly call `bd hooks run <name>` — but
`git config core.hooksPath` is set to `.husky/_` in both repos. Git therefore runs
husky's hooks and NEVER runs the beads shims. The Dolt<->git sync does not happen:
no pre-commit/pre-push JSONL export, no post-checkout/post-merge re-import.

WHY IT LOOKS HEALTHY (the trap): `bd hooks list` reports
    ✓ pre-commit: installed (version )
    ✓ post-merge: installed (version )   ... x5
Note the EMPTY version string. Contrast the umbrella after its fix, which reports
"installed (shim 1.1.2)". bd appears to be confirming the shim FILES exist rather
than confirming git will actually execute them, so its green is not evidence the
sync runs. Do not trust `bd hooks list` alone in a repo that uses husky.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE: at sweep time BOTH repos had uncommitted
`.beads/issues.jsonl` (`MM` = staged+unstaged) — exactly the drift signature you
get when Dolt moves and the JSONL mirror is never auto-exported.

DO NOT FIX BY REPOINTING core.hooksPath. That is what the umbrella needed (its
path named a stale pre-rename directory), but here `.husky/_` is CORRECT and
load-bearing: husky runs lint-staged (eslint+prettier) plus escape-scan in the
compiler, and lint-staged plus verify-policy-hash.sh (the policy ruleset hash-pin
gate, 036-AT-THRT C10 / bead dmj.1) in the registrar. Repointing to .beads/hooks
would silently DISABLE those Testing-SOP gates — trading a bead-sync bug for a
test-enforcement hole.

CORRECT FIX — CHAIN, don't replace. Keep core.hooksPath=.husky/_ and have each
husky hook also invoke beads, e.g. append to .husky/pre-commit (and the
pre-push / post-checkout / post-merge / prepare-commit-msg equivalents):

    # beads Dolt<->git sync (chained; core.hooksPath is owned by husky)
    if command -v bd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      BD_GIT_HOOK=1 bd hooks run pre-commit "$@" || true
    fi

Design decisions to make while implementing:
  1. Fail-open (`|| true`) or fail-closed? The beads shims themselves wrap the
     call in a timeout and no-op when bd is absent, so fail-open matches upstream
     behavior. A failing export should not block a commit.
  2. Prefer sourcing/delegating to `.beads/hooks/<name>` over copy-pasting the
     shim body, so `bd hooks install` upgrades keep working (the umbrella's shims
     were stale at v1.0.4 while bd was 1.1.2 — see compile-then-govern PR #73).
  3. `core.hooksPath` is LOCAL git config and NOT committed, so the chaining edit
     must live in the tracked husky hook files to help anyone else's clone.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - In each repo: make a trivial commit and confirm the JSONL export fires
    (`git status` shows .beads/issues.jsonl updated by the hook, not by hand).
  - `git config --get core.hooksPath` still returns `.husky/_`.
  - husky's existing gates still run (verify escape-scan / verify-policy-hash.sh
    still execute on a policy-touching commit).
  - Commit the drifted `.beads/issues.jsonl` in both repos once sync works.

SINGLE-WRITER: both repos had in-flight work at sweep time (compiler on
feat/e06.5-governed-freshness-incremental; registrar on
feat/b1-b2-reranker-and-seam-firewall). This bead was filed WITHOUT touching
either tree. Hand to the owning per-repo agent.

Related prior art: the umbrella hit the same class of bug from a different cause
(stale pre-rename absolute path) — fixed in
intent-solutions-io/bobs-big-brain-umbrella PR #73, which also documents that a
first `bd hooks install` MATERIALIZED the stale path rather than repointing.

title: Investigate the 13x reference-category growth in curated_memories and decide whether the daily compile loop is over-capturing
description:
FINDING (evidence, 2026-07-29): regenerating the umbrella's live-brain stats block
(bin/teamkb-systemmap.sh -> 000-docs/005-AT-ARCH §0, umbrella PR #72) showed the brain
grew ~4x in the 13 days from 2026-07-16 to 2026-07-29, and the growth is NOT evenly
distributed across categories:

  ~/.teamkb total        859M  -> 3.4G
  teamkb.db               18M  -> 245M
  qmd-index/ (derived)    39M  -> 527M
  candidates             2312  -> 17539
  curated_memories       2302  -> 17377  (active 10184 / superseded 6501 / deprecated 681 / archived 11)
  audit_events           2618  -> 24602  (v1 872 unchanged / v2 1746 -> 23730)

  BY CATEGORY:
    reference        1260 -> 16221   (13x)
    pattern           576 ->   586   (+10)
    troubleshooting   315 ->   341   (+26)
    architecture       78 ->   103   (+25)
    decision           32 ->    62   (+30)
    convention         27 ->    47   (+20)
    onboarding         14 ->    17   (+3)

WHY THIS LOOKS WRONG: every category except `reference` grew by tens. `reference` grew
by ~15,000. A brain does not genuinely learn 15k new reference facts in 13 days while
learning only 10 new patterns. The shape says the daily compile loop is mass-promoting
low-value reference material rather than the corpus actually getting richer.

Corroborating: superseded (6501) + deprecated (681) is ~41% of curated_memories, which
is a lot of churn; and qmd-index/ ballooning 39M -> 527M is the retrieval cost of
carrying that volume. Retrieval is BM25-on-qmd today, so index size is a direct
precision/latency tax on every brain_search.

SCOPE: investigate, then decide. Do NOT bulk-delete memories as a first move.
  1. Characterize: sample the `reference` rows created in the window; are they
     near-duplicates, chunk-splits of the same source, or genuinely distinct?
  2. Attribute: which writer produced them (teamkb-compile-daily.sh vs brain_capture
     vs a backfill)? Cross-check against the 8-rule governance policy completed
     2026-07-17 (see auto-memory live-brain-schema-v9-and-complete-policy) — did a
     policy rule change on/around 07-17 open a floodgate?
  3. Decide: tighten the promotion rule, add a dedupe/paraphrase gate, or accept the
     volume and reindex. Whichever way, record it as a decision record.

NOT IN SCOPE: the brain-freshness/self-heal loop itself (that is epic
bd_000-projects-gybo) and qmd version-drift alerting (bd_000-projects-e6ov). This bead
is specifically about CAPTURE VOLUME AND QUALITY, which those two do not cover.

EVIDENCE LINK: umbrella PR #72 (docs/refresh-live-brain-stats) carries the measured
before/after table in its body and in the commit message.

title: Track A — scheduled reindex + self-heal so promoted memories can never sit unsearchable
description:
TRACK A — Scheduled reindex + self-heal. OWNER: registrar agent (writes the script + compile-gate) + Mission Control (installs/enables the timer). BLOCKED ON: registrar -> origin/main prereq.

THE GAP: index refresh is opportunistic-inside-runGovern ONLY — no standalone timer, and ~/bin/teamkb-compile-daily.sh makes no reindex/canary call. If the inline `qmd update` fails, the compile still "succeeds," leaving promoted-but-unindexed memories with nothing to catch it (the exact drift that started this). Exit-0 is not success (intent-os doctrine).

REUSE — DO NOT REBUILD (all in bobs-big-brain-registrar/packages/qmd-adapter/src/):
- cli.ts — already exposes `reindex` and `canary --heal` subcommands.
- canary/search-canary.ts — unhealthy -> reindex -> recheck (the self-heal primitive).
- reindex/reindex.ts — ensureCollections() -> update().
- health/health-check.ts — checkHealth incl. stalenessSeconds (D2 gauge, currently measured-not-actioned).

APPROACH (registrar agent writes; enforcement travels in-repo):
1. Thin wrapper bbb-reindex-heal.sh in the registrar repo bin/ (deployed to ~/bin) that runs `qmd-adapter canary --heal` for BOTH tenants (intent-solutions, local) using the now-correct 2.5.3 on PATH. Source ~/bin/lib/notify-lib.sh and `arm_fail_trap "bbb-reindex-heal" ""` so it pages #cron-failures on failure and touches .beat/.ok.
2. Add a post-compile gate to teamkb-compile-daily.sh: after govern, assert the index actually refreshed (outcome-verification, not exit-0), and heal if not.
3. A systemd USER timer for bbb-reindex-heal (install driven from MC), scheduled after the nightly compile/index window.

VERIFY: promote a memory -> run the heal wrapper -> brain_search finds it; then simulate an index skip (interrupt `qmd update` mid-govern) and confirm the scheduled heal detects the DB-vs-index staleness and repairs it.

ROUTE:
- registrar agent: the wrapper bbb-reindex-heal.sh + the compile-gate in teamkb-compile-daily.sh.
- Mission Control: install/enable the systemd user timer (box/systemd action).
HAND-OFF NOTE: at deploy, seed the .beat and register in the liveness sweep WHEN the OUT-of-scope intent-os follow-up runs (registry.json + automation-liveness-sweep.sh row + mission-control/automations.md row + spine-c67 attach) — so it isn't a silent-failure landmine in the interim.

title: Wire Bob's Big Brain fully current + self-updating — the brain-freshness loop
description:
The brain-freshness loop: keep Bob's Big Brain searchable, dense, and current on its own, so a promoted memory can never sit unsearchable and the plugin runtime never lags the engine.

WHY THIS EXISTS (root cause, recon-confirmed): memories were promoted + anchored but not searchable because brain_govern's index-refresh step silently failed — every runtime shelled to the bare command `qmd`, which resolved to ~/.bun/bin/qmd v2.0.1 while the pinned @tobilu/qmd@2.5.3 sat unreachable in node_modules/.bin. The govern index step ran against the wrong qmd. Jeremy already closed the linchpin from Mission Control (single-writer): global qmd bumped 2.0.1 -> 2.5.3, brain_search validated returning the target memory at score 1.0 on the forward-compatible index (no forced rebuild, fully reversible — the index is derived from the governed store).

THIS EPIC = the remaining stay-current loop, and it BUILDS NOTHING here — it is a spec + routing map. Each child is a hand-off to the owning per-repo agent (registrar / plugin) or Mission Control. Do NOT write in a halted agent's tree — single-writer per repo. Box/systemd actions are driven from Mission Control.

SCOPE:
- IN: (A) scheduled reindex/self-heal so promoted memories can never sit unsearchable; (B) wire the dense arm on for real; (C) keep the plugin runtime current with the engine.
- OUT (explicit follow-ups, per Jeremy 2026-07-26): registering the new automation into intent-os's model (ops/automation/registry.json + automation-liveness-sweep.sh row + mission-control/automations.md row + spine-c67 attach); the B3 cross-system sync (GH<->Plane<->Beads<->Dolt, intent-os doc 121); an auto-rebundle CI gate.
- DONE: qmd version bump (Jeremy); version-drift alerting -> sibling bead bd_000-projects-e6ov (registrar agent, labels brain/cross-session/qmd).

DEPENDENCY ORDER:
  registrar -> origin/main  (PREREQ, registrar agent)
        |__ Track A  (reindex/self-heal — registrar script + MC timer)
        |__ Track B  (dense default-on + full-corpus index — registrar)
                    |__ Track C  (plugin rebundle + currency — plugin agent)

END-TO-END DEFINITION OF DONE (testable):
1. Never-unsearchable: save a memory (/brain-save), let a govern run, brain_search finds it same-day; force an index skip and the scheduled heal (Track A) repairs it within its interval.
2. Dense live: a semantic/paraphrase query returns the right hit through the plugin (Track B/C), matching the measured 0.34->0.96 gain.
3. Currency: brain_status healthy; plugin runtime 1.2.0 consistent; no 0.1.6 ghost; gsb.lock.json current.
4. Self-reporting: the reindex/heal job pages #cron-failures on failure (notify-lib), so a future break pings instead of being found mid-session.

Related sibling (already filed, DONE-routed): bd_000-projects-e6ov (qmd version-drift check + Slack alerting, registrar agent).

title: Prevent unapproved AI labels from entering canonical BBB memory
design: Cross-reference the BBB anti-AI-leak guard. Critical for the doctrine.
acceptance_criteria: Refusal service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) reject any ingestion attempt whose source_type ∈ {ai-proposal, unverified}, (2) log the rejection attempt with the requester's identity + the rejected object's id, (3) integration test that asserts the refusal works.

title: Implement governed ingestion of accepted failure patterns into BBB
design: Default to the existing BBB MCP (`~/.grok/config.toml` or similar) for the ingestion transport.
acceptance_criteria: Ingestion service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept an accepted annotation + its evidence_receipt_id, (2) emit a BBBKnowledgeEntry (C15 schema) with citation_trace_ids + citation_evidence_receipt_ids, (3) require AGP-mediated authorization (H3 + H4), (4) integration test that asserts AI-proposed-only annotations are refused.

title: Define which accepted evaluation findings become institutional knowledge
design: Cross-reference C15 (BBB ingestion contract).
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-G1-bbb-inclusions.md`. Must declare: (1) the criteria for an evaluation finding to qualify (must be a human-accepted annotation + a signed evidence receipt + a non-AI-proposed provenance), (2) the inclusion procedure (which BBB entry type, which TTL, which citation chain), (3) the exclusion criteria (ephemeral traces, AI-proposed labels, raw evidence payloads). Owner sign-off required.
notes:
Group G — Bob's Big Brain and organizational learning.
BBB refuses AI-proposed entries without an intervening human-accepted annotation (G3). Citation chain mandatory (G4). Lifecycle: expiry + supersession + correction (G5).

title: Add Mission Control readiness and risk views
design: Build on the existing intent-os Mission Control architecture. The views are derived projections; no new domain logic.
acceptance_criteria: New Mission Control views: (1) 'Trace Intel Coverage' (per-repo gap status), (2) 'Annotation Throughput' (accepted/rejected/pending per repo), (3) 'Taxonomy Drift' (per-repo current-vs-latest), (4) 'Evidence Validity' (per-repo valid/invalid receipts). Each view has a Mission Control route, a render spec, and a test. Acceptance: all four views render without error in a dev Mission Control instance + the views load in <2 seconds with 10k repos.

title: Reconcile or retire duplicated existing evaluation components
design: Per the deterministic-first doctrine: never deprecate without proof of equivalence. The runtime check is the migration's safety net.
acceptance_criteria: Per-entry replacement plan in `000-docs/trace-intel-E8-replacement-proof.md`. For every duplicate identified in A5/A6: declare retired component, replacement component, migration guide, rollback plan, and a runtime check proving both implementations agree on a fixture set for ≥7 consecutive days. Owner sign-off required. No retirement may happen until the runtime agreement is proven.

title: Integrate signed evidence with Evidence Bench
design: Evidence Bench is the single source of truth for receipts. Cross-reference `bd_000-projects-0r8m` (signed evidence reports) and `bd_000-projects-h08j.7` (verification, currently DEFERRED).
acceptance_criteria: Integration PR connecting the evidence producer (D21) with Evidence Bench. Evidence Bench must accept the EvidenceReceipt (C13) as an ingest artifact, store it, expose verification, and link it to the EvalRun. Integration test producing 10 receipts and verifying all 10 are queryable + verifiable in Evidence Bench.

title: Integrate evaluation outcomes with rollout-gate
design: Deferred Evidence Bundle signature verification (`bd_000-projects-h08j.7`) becomes unblocked by this integration.
acceptance_criteria: Integration PR into `intent-eval-platform/intent-rollout-gate`. The rollout-gate must consume the EvidenceReceipt + RolloutDecision (C12/C13) and use them to gate merges. Integration test that runs rollout-gate with a fixture EvalRun + signed receipt + decision and asserts the merge is blocked on fail, allowed on pass. Cross-reference existing rollout-gate lanes `bd_000-projects-444u` and `bd_000-projects-1332`.

title: Register the capability inside the Intent Eval Platform estate
design: If C17 chose a new repo, this bead creates it; otherwise it registers the capability in the existing IEP estate. Cross-reference the IEP existing capability manifest pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Capability registered in the IEP estate at `intent-eval-platform/intent-eval-lab/000-docs/trace-intel-E1-registration.md`. Must list: owning repo (per C17), capability name (TraceIntelligence), capability version (semver), interfaces exposed (per C1-C19), Mission Control readiness+risk view (per F12), and a link to the A8 audit report. Owner sign-off required.
notes:
Group E — Intent Eval Platform integration.
Each integration depends on the corresponding D-bead. E8 (retire duplicates) requires replacement proof: 7 consecutive days of runtime agreement between old + new components.

title: Implement role-based access and sensitive-data controls
design: Disclosure-gate's hard-fail redaction set is the baseline. Cross-reference the IEP disclosure-gate.sh for the secret pattern list.
acceptance_criteria: Access-control service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) enforce the AGP-mediated authorization for every operation (H1-H3), (2) enforce the C19 deletion procedure (owner approval + audit log + tombstone metadata retained 1y), (3) redact secrets from trace content at ingest boundary (using the patterns from the IEP disclosure-gate hard-fail set as the default), (4) integration test that ingests a trace with a fake-secret, asserts the secret is redacted before canonical storage, and asserts an AGP-fail returns 403.

title: Implement signed evidence production
design: Use ed25519 + hash chain per C13 default. The signing key lives in the AGP-controlled keystore (per C16). The Evidence Bench is the downstream consumer; the producer writes to the bench via the bench's intake API.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence producer in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept any canonical-state object (EvalRun, AnnotationEvent, dataset version, taxonomy migration, regression case), (2) emit an EvidenceReceipt (C13 schema) with content_hash, signature_value, signing_key_id, chain_prev_receipt_id, policy_version, (3) persist the receipt, (4) expose GET /evidence/{id} that returns the receipt + signature verification, (5) integration test that produces 10 chained receipts and verifies the chain from receipt 1..10.

title: Implement evaluator-generation workflow (regression-cases → executable evals)
design: Cross-reference JRig's existing run-output schema (`bd_000-projects-214c`). JRig is the default binary-skill framework; pytest is for non-binary evals.
acceptance_criteria: Evaluator-generation workflow in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept a list of regression_case_ids + a target framework (jrig | pytest | custom), (2) emit an executable eval per case using the chosen framework, (3) emit an EvalRun record per execution (C11 schema) with score + score_breakdown + policy_version, (4) emit a signed evidence receipt per EvalRun, (5) integration test with 10 regression cases + verifies 10 EvalRuns + 10 evidence receipts with hash-chained links.

title: Implement regression-case generator
design: The human-accepted requirement is what enforces the AI-must-be-approved rule at the regression layer. Without it, the system would regress to AI-proposed-only behavior over time.
acceptance_criteria: Regression generator in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept a dataset_version_id, (2) emit one RegressionCase per source annotation_id (C10 schema), (3) require the source annotation to be human-accepted (no AI-proposed-only annotations can generate regression cases), (4) emit a signed evidence receipt per regression case, (5) integration test with 100 accepted annotations + 10 rejected ones + verifies only 100 regression cases are emitted.

title: Implement dataset versioning and reproducibility
design: Reproducibility requires the source annotations to be immutable. Annotation events (C4) are append-only — the source never changes, so rebuild is well-defined.
acceptance_criteria: Versioning service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) on every new EvalDataset, emit an EvalDatasetVersion (C9) with breaking_change_summary if applicable, (2) expose GET /datasets/{id}/versions that returns the version history, (3) expose POST /datasets/{id}/rebuild that, given a version_id, rebuilds the exact dataset bytes from the declared inputs and asserts content_hash equality, (4) integration test creating 3 versions + rebuilding each.

title: Implement dataset builder
design: Reproducibility_uri: pointer to the source annotations + the taxonomy_version + the sampling_policy_id + a Dolt commit hash (or equivalent).
acceptance_criteria: Dataset service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept a list of accepted annotation_ids + a name + a description, (2) emit an EvalDataset per C9 schema with content_hash, reproducibility_uri, annotation_source_ids, taxonomy_version, sampling_policy_id, (3) store the dataset, (4) integration test that builds a dataset from 100 fixture accepted annotations and verifies content_hash matches the rebuilt bytes.

title: Implement taxonomy versioning and migration
design: Migration is forward-only by default. Reversal requires a new migration rule. Cross-reference the existing iel-E15b work.
acceptance_criteria: Migration service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) on a MAJOR taxonomy version bump, generate a migration rule (rename, merge, split, deprecate) for every node in the prior version, (2) apply the migration to all historical annotations pointing at superseded nodes, (3) emit a signed evidence receipt for the migration (C13), (4) integration test that simulates a MAJOR bump + 10 affected annotations + verifies the migration is reversible from the signed receipt.

title: Implement failure-taxonomy registry
design: Use the existing IEP event-taxonomy work in `bd_000-projects-fqtm` as a starting point if appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy registry in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) store TaxonomyNode + TaxonomyVersion per C7 schema, (2) enforce that any new node requires a taxonomy-editor role (H4), (3) expose CRUD APIs with versioning, (4) expose GET /taxonomy/{version}/tree (full hierarchy), (5) integration test that creates a node, supersedes it, and verifies both versions are queryable.

title: Implement human acceptance and rejection workflow
design: Cross-reference the IEP summarize.py reviewer-override pattern. The signed receipt is the proof that a human approved; AI cannot sign.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance workflow in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept the reviewer's accept|reject|revise decision (C4), (2) on accept: write the AnnotationRecord with human-accepted state and emit a signed evidence receipt (C13), (3) on reject: write the rejection audit entry with the rejecting reviewer's identity, (4) on revise: open a new annotation cycle (never mutate the prior record), (5) integration test covering all three branches + verifying the signed receipt for accept.

title: Implement AI annotation-proposal service
design: Proposal service is a separate API endpoint from the annotation backend (D8). The two cannot share a database table. Cross-reference the IEP summarize.py proposal + override pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept a batch of trace_ids + the current taxonomy_version + a model_id (C6), (2) emit a ProposalObject per C6 schema (model_id + prompt_hash + confidence), (3) store the proposals in a proposal-only data plane (NEVER in canonical state), (4) require AGP-mediated authorization for every emit (H3), (5) integration test that emits 10 proposals and verifies the canonical AnnotationRecord table is empty until human acceptance.

title: Implement annotation audit log
design: Audit log IS the signed-evidence chain. Cross-reference C13. Same signing key custodian as the rest of the program.
acceptance_criteria: Audit-log service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) persist every annotation event as an immutable, hash-chained entry per C13/C4, (2) expose GET /audit-log?annotation_id=X that returns the full chain, (3) reject any attempt to UPDATE or DELETE an audit-log entry (only append is allowed), (4) integration test that simulates 100 events and verifies the chain validates.

title: Implement annotation backend (storage + state transitions)
design: Storage: Dolt or Postgres + JSONB per C17 choice. Use append-only AnnotationEvent log; AnnotationRecord is the current state projection.
acceptance_criteria: Annotation service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) persist AnnotationRecord + AnnotationEvent per C4 schema (CQRS separation), (2) enforce state-transition rules (a rejected record cannot be re-accepted without a new annotation event), (3) require AGP-mediated authorization for every state transition (H2), (4) integration test that simulates a full annotation lifecycle (create → revise → accept → supersede) and verifies the audit log is correct. No annotation UI yet (D9).

title: Implement trace lineage and content hashing
design: Lineage MUST be append-only. Cross-reference the Evidence Bench's hash-chained receipts pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Lineage service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) compute content_hash (sha256 of canonical JSON) at ingest, (2) record the lineage chain (trace_id → derived cluster_id → annotation_id → dataset_version → regression_case_id → eval_run_id → evidence_receipt_id), (3) expose a GET /lineage/{trace_id} API that returns the full chain, (4) integration test that pushes a synthetic trace and verifies the chain endpoint returns at least 3 levels deep.

title: Implement trace validation and rejection handling
design: Quarantine is a real table, not just a log line. Owner-reviewable. Cross-reference the IEP fail-closed posture.
acceptance_criteria: Validation layer in the same repo as D2. Must: (1) validate every incoming trace against the C1 JSON Schema, (2) on validation failure, emit a structured rejection event (per C19's deletion architecture, rejections are NOT silently dropped — they go to a quarantine table for owner review), (3) include unit tests for at least 5 invalid-trace shapes (missing field, wrong type, content_hash mismatch, expired timestamp, malformed JSON). Owner review of quarantine table is a weekly cron per J13.

title: Implement normalized trace storage
design: Use Dolt as the default storage if C17 chooses IEP-owned; otherwise use Postgres + JSONB. Cross-reference B7 research on dataset versioning — Dolt's commit-hash model fits naturally with the C2 content_hash requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Storage layer at the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) persist the trace_id (UUIDv7, primary key), the content_hash, the canonical JSON, the raw input (immutable), and the lineage metadata, (2) enforce the C2 retention rules (raw + canonical both retained ≥365d), (3) expose a query API supporting time-range + trace_id + content_hash lookups, (4) expose a write API that rejects any record failing C1 schema validation. Must include unit + integration tests including the retention rule.

title: Implement trace-ingestion adapter framework (one adapter per source)
design: Vendor-neutral adapters must accept the source's native shape and emit the C1-normalized trace. Treat the Claude Code native OTel path (`bd_000-projects-awuw.2`) as the canonical first adapter. The framework must register adapter failures via AGP policy + emit a diagnostic event to Mission Control; never silently drop traces.
acceptance_criteria: Repository at the IEP placement chosen in C17 (default: intent-eval-platform/intent-eval-core or a new IEP-owned capability repo if C17 decides otherwise) contains: (1) a base `TraceIngestionAdapter` interface in TypeScript OR Python (pick one per the architectural ADR), (2) at least 3 reference adapters implementing that interface (one for Claude Code native OTel, one for file-log scraping, one for HTTP push), (3) unit tests for each adapter ≥ 80% line coverage, (4) an integration test that pushes a synthetic trace through every adapter and asserts the trace matches C1's schema. The integration test must be runnable via `pnpm test` or `pytest tests/test_ingestion.py`. No production deploy in this bead.
notes:
Group D — Foundational implementation plan.
Implementation ordered by data flow: ingest → store → cluster → sample → annotate → AI proposals → human acceptance → taxonomy → datasets → regression → evals → evidence → access controls. AI proposals NEVER mutate canonical state without human approval.

title: Produce the final architecture ADR set (entry gate for Group D)
design: Use the MADR template (https://adr.github.io/madr/). Each ADR cites the underlying C-bead by ID. Owner review is the close criterion.
acceptance_criteria: ADR set at `000-docs/trace-intel-architecture-adr-index.md` with one ADR per C1-C19 contract (decisions + context + consequences + alternatives considered). Index must include: ADR title, owner-signed status, links to the contract spec. The ADR set is the formal entry gate for Group D — no implementation bead may begin until C20 is closed AND A8 is closed AND B12 is closed AND C17 is owner-signed.
notes: ENTRY GATE: this bead's close + A8 close + B12 close + C17 owner-signed = formal go/no-go for Group D.

title: Define security, privacy, access, and deletion architecture
design: Cross-reference the existing intent-os SOPS + age secrets standard (per `~/CLAUDE.md` § 'Initiative: SOPS + age secrets standard'). Threat model must include annotation leakage + evidence-receipt leakage as distinct concerns.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C19-security-architecture.md`. Must declare: (1) authentication mechanism (OAuth? AGP-issued tokens?), (2) authorization model (per-repository ACL? per-agent ACL? per-classification ACL?), (3) encryption-at-rest posture (per-store), (4) encryption-in-transit posture (mTLS? Tailscale-only?), (5) deletion procedure (owner approval + audit log + tombstone metadata retained), (6) the threat model this architecture defends against (cite B10 research). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define development, staging, and production placement
design: Default to VPS-resident for any new capability per the prod VPS posture in `~/CLAUDE.md`. Cross-reference the existing intent-os deployment topology + the 36-container VPS estate.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C18-environment-placement.md`. Must declare (1) where dev/staging/prod traces are stored (per repo: a separate namespace or a separate cluster?), (2) how the signed-evidence producer runs (library import, microservice, GH Action — owner picks one), (3) how the annotation backend is deployed (self-host on the VPS alongside the IEP estate? a new container?), (4) how the regression generator is triggered (manual? CI? scheduled?), (5) data-deletion procedure (owner approval + audit log entry + retention of tombstone metadata for 1 year). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define repository ownership and component boundaries (placement decisions)
design: Default placement: IEP-owned for evaluation logic + datasets + evidence production; intent-os for projections + Mission Control; AGP for authority + policy; BBB for cited knowledge. New repos allowed only if no existing repo fits. Owner-gated.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C17-ownership-boundaries.md` with an owner-signed placement table. For every component in the architecture (trace ingestion, trace storage, clustering, sampling, annotation, AI-proposal, human-approval, taxonomy, dataset, regression, eval, evidence, rollout-gate projection, BBB ingestion, AGP enforcement), the spec MUST declare: owning repo (existing or new + owner decision), external dependencies, and a one-sentence rationale. Owner sign-off required before any D-series implementation may begin.

title: Define AGP authority and policy boundaries
design: Cross-reference existing AGP authority rules in the intent-solutions-io estate. The policy_version field is what makes every signed evidence receipt 'verifiable against the policy that was active at signing time.'
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C16-agp-policy.md`. Must declare: (1) the set of authority-required actions (read trace, propose annotation, accept annotation, mutate taxonomy, generate eval, promote eval to gate, sign evidence receipt), (2) the actor identity required for each (human-reviewer-id, ai-proposer-id, evidence-signer-id, etc), (3) the fail-closed posture (if AGP is unreachable OR policy validation fails, the operation MUST be refused, not skipped), (4) policy versioning rule (policy_version field on every AGP-mediated op). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define Bob's Big Brain knowledge-ingestion contracts
design: BBB refuses AI-proposed entries without an intervening human-accepted annotation. Expiry_at enforces 'no permanent memory without periodic review'.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C15-bbb-ingestion-contract.md`. JSON Schema for BBBKnowledgeEntry (entry_id, source_type enum [annotation, evidence-receipt, manual], source_id, taxonomy_version, content_hash, expiry_at, supersedes_entry_id, citation_trace_ids array, citation_evidence_receipt_ids array, ingested_at, ingested_by URI). Must require: source_type ∈ {annotation, evidence-receipt, manual} — NEVER ai-proposal, and expiry_at (no permanent BBB entries from this program; lifetime capped). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define Mission Control projection contracts
design: Mission Control does NOT compute these projections — it consumes them. The IEP-owned capability must expose APIs (or Dolt views) that Mission Control polls. Cross-reference the Mission Control readiness + risk view pattern in F12.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C14-mc-projection-contract.md`. JSON Schema for: (1) CoverageProjection (repo, agent_id, trace_count_last_7d, annotation_count_last_7d, gap_status enum [none, partial, missing]), (2) TaxonomyDriftProjection (repo, current_taxonomy_version, latest_taxonomy_version, drift_status enum [current, drifting, unknown]), (3) EvidenceValidityProjection (repo, valid_receipts_last_30d, invalid_receipts_last_30d, validity_status enum [healthy, degraded, broken]). Must reference IEP-owned projection data sources (not local copies). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define signed evidence-receipt contracts
design: Use hash-chained receipts (each receipt references the previous) so tampering with any historical receipt invalidates every downstream receipt. Cross-reference B9 research for signature algorithm choice. Default to ed25519 + a hash chain. Evidence Bundle signature verification (`bd_000-projects-h08j.7`) becomes unblocked when this contract ships.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C13-evidence-receipt-contract.md`. JSON Schema for EvidenceReceipt (receipt_id, content_hash, signature_algorithm enum [ed25519, rsa-pss, ecdsa-p256], signature_value base64, signing_key_id, policy_version, chain_prev_receipt_id, created_at, payload object). Must require: chain_prev_receipt_id (for hash-chained audit), signing_key_id (for key custodian lookup), and content_hash (for tamper detection). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define rollout-decision contracts
design: Overrides are explicit accountability, not silent bypass. Cross-reference rollout-gate's existing decision schema and gate-result/v1 predicate URI pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C12-rollout-decision-contract.md`. JSON Schema for RolloutDecision (decision_id, repo, commit, policy_version, evidence_receipt_ids array, gate_result enum [pass, fail, advisory], decided_at, decided_by URI, override_reason optional, override_by URI optional). Override is allowed but MUST be recorded with the override-actor identity and reason. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define evaluation-run and score contracts
design: Score_breakdown breaks the single score into per-attribute scores (e.g., pass_rate, false_positive_rate, latency_p95) to support future drill-down. Cross-reference JRig's existing run-output schema.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C11-eval-run-contract.md`. JSON Schema for EvalRun (run_id, dataset_id, dataset_version, framework, framework_version, agent_id, agent_version, started_at, ended_at, score, score_breakdown object, policy_version, evidence_receipt_id, content_hash). Must require evidence_receipt_id (per C13) so every EvalRun is verifiable. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define generated regression-case contracts
design: The human-accepted-annotation source requirement is what enforces the AI-proposal-must-be-human-approved rule at the regression layer. Cross-reference D19 (implement regression-case generator) and D20 (run them).
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C10-regression-contract.md`. JSON Schema for RegressionCase (case_id, source_dataset_id, source_annotation_id, expected_outcome, framework enum [jrig, pytest, custom], framework_version, assertion_text, created_at). Must require: source_annotation_id (regression cases are traceable to a human-accepted annotation) and source_dataset_id (the dataset the regression case is drawn from). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define evaluation dataset and dataset-version contracts
design: Use Dolt commit hash as the content_hash default if the dataset is stored in Dolt. Use IPFS CID or a similar content-addressed URI as the alternative. Cross-reference B7 research for storage options.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C9-dataset-contract.md`. JSON Schema for: (1) EvalDataset (dataset_id, dataset_version, name, description, annotation_source_ids array, taxonomy_version, sampling_policy_id, created_at, content_hash, reproducibility_uri), (2) EvalDatasetVersion (same shape minus reproducibility_uri, plus supersedes_dataset_version, breaking_change_summary). The contract MUST require content_hash + reproducibility_uri so any party can rebuild the exact dataset bytes. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define sampling-policy and sampling-decision contracts
design: Determinism via params_hash: the SamplingDecision is reproducible by re-running the policy with the same params. Cross-reference B4 research for which strategy fits which situation; this contract just defines the wire format.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C8-sampling-contract.md`. JSON Schema for: (1) SamplingPolicy (policy_id, strategy enum [uniform, uncertainty, diversity, coverage-gap, committee-disagreement], batch_size, target_count, policy_version), (2) SamplingDecision (decision_id, policy_id, sampled_trace_ids, params_hash, decided_at, decided_by URI). The contract MUST be deterministic: given the same policy + same input trace set + same params_hash, the same SamplingDecision is produced. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define failure-taxonomy and taxonomy-version contracts
design: Use semver for TaxonomyVersion. Breaking changes (node shape, label rename) bump MAJOR; additive changes bump MINOR; clarifications bump PATCH. Cross-reference the existing iel-E15b event taxonomy work (`bd_000-projects-fqtm`); treat this contract as an extension, not a replacement.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C7-taxonomy-contract.md`. JSON Schema for TaxonomyNode (node_id, parent_node_id, label, definition, evidence_required_type enum [trace, annotation, eval, external], created_at, supersedes_node_id, supersession_reason) + TaxonomyVersion (version, release_date, supersedes_version, breaking_change_summary). Must include a migration rule for old annotations pointing at a superseded node. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define AI-proposed annotation contracts
design: AI proposals must NEVER mutate canonical state. They are a proposal-only data plane. Cross-reference the existing IEP summarize.py pattern (proposal + reviewer override) and the AGP H1-H6 fail-closed posture.
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C6-ai-proposal-contract.md`. Must declare: (1) the proposal-object schema (trace_id, proposed_taxonomy_node_id, proposed_label_value, confidence, model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, created_at), (2) the human-acceptance contract (a human reviewer MUST issue an AnnotationEvent with decision=accept before the proposal can become an accepted AnnotationRecord), (3) the proposal-rejection audit (proposals that are rejected are recorded with the rejecting reviewer's identity, never deleted), (4) a confidence threshold above which the proposal is auto-shown to reviewers (default: ≥ 0.7 — owner-overridable). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define human reviewer identity and approval contracts
design: Default to BBB identity for self-host consistency. Cross-reference the AGP authority model in H1-H6. Reviewer authority levels map to AGP roles. The co-sign rule for taxonomy mutations is owner-gated (default to N=2).
acceptance_criteria: Spec at `000-docs/trace-intel-C5-reviewer-identity.md`. Must declare: (1) the reviewer-identity provider (BBB identity, AGP-issued, or external OAuth — owner must pick one), (2) approval-as-decision vs approval-as-co-sign (does a single reviewer suffice, or are N reviewers required for taxonomy mutations?), (3) reviewer authority levels (default, taxonomy-editor, dataset-editor, evidence-editor), (4) how reviewer identity is preserved across system boundaries (signing keys, federation, etc). Owner sign-off required.

title: Define annotation record and annotation-event contracts
design: AnnotationEvent is the audit log; AnnotationRecord is the current canonical state. Use CQRS-style separation so the audit log is append-only. Cite RFC 7807-style error responses for invalid state transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Schema at `000-docs/trace-intel-C4-annotation-contract.md`. JSON Schemas for: (1) AnnotationRecord (annotation_id UUIDv7, trace_id, taxonomy_node_id, label_value, confidence, annotator_id URI, created_at, decision: accept|reject|revise, free_text optional, evidence_receipt_id optional), (2) AnnotationEvent (the immutable log entry: any create, update, retract, supersede, accept, or reject action — must reference the AnnotationRecord it acts on). The schema MUST distinguish 'AI-proposed' annotations from 'human-accepted' annotations via a decision-state field. Owner sign-off required.

title: Define cluster and similarity-result contracts
design: The stability re-run field is what makes the cluster reproducible across the deterministic-first doctrine. Cite sklearn's HDBSCAN stability metric and the Leiden algorithm's modularity guarantee as the basis for the algorithm-version + params_hash requirement.
acceptance_criteria: Schema at `000-docs/trace-intel-C3-cluster-contract.md`. title: Audit intent-solutions-io GitHub repositories for trace / evaluation / annotation / evidence components

Per `~/CLAUDE.md` ownership rules, private repos require the org-admin scope; verify gh auth has the right visibility before claiming a repo is missing. If gh auth lacks the scope, STOP and surface the gap as a blocker; do not list private repos as 'missing.'
acceptance_criteria: Same artifact shape as A1, for github.com/intent-solutions-io. Deliverable: `000-docs/trace-intel-A2-intent-solutions-io-audit.md` committed to intent-eval-platform/intent-eval-lab. Must include, per repo: commit count + last SHA + license + visibility, trace/telemetry/annotation/eval/evidence/taxonomy code paths, related GH Actions, release tags, missing-repo API response codes. Owner sign-off required before A3 may begin.

title: Audit jeremylongshore GitHub repositories for trace / evaluation / annotation / evidence components
design: Use the GitHub REST API via the authenticated `gh` CLI. Run a single bash script that paginates /orgs/jeremylongshore/repos (or /users/jeremylongshore/repos) and writes JSON, then a deterministic jq filter that selects the fields above. Defer tool selection for the audit itself (just use gh). DO NOT clone repos in this bead — listing + metadata only. Cloning is A3's job. DO NOT use any feature flag, beta endpoint, or unreleased GitHub API. NO fabrication of file paths — every claimed file path must be backed by either `gh api .../contents/<path>` returning 200, or a clone + grep in A3.
acceptance_criteria: Audit report delivered as `000-docs/trace-intel-A1-jeremylongshore-audit.md` and committed to `intent-eval-platform/intent-eval-lab`. Group A — Estate audit and current-state discovery.
These 8 beads establish ground truth before any architecture decision. Every claim in later beads must cite an A-series artifact. Owner sign-off on A8 is the formal entry gate to Group B.

title: Governed Trace Intelligence and Evaluation Learning Loop
description:
# Governed Trace Intelligence and Evaluation Learning Loop

## Objective

Create a future research and implementation program that closes the loop from
agent traces to evaluation decisions to signed evidence, governed by Intent
Solutions' deterministic-first principles. The program must answer five
questions for any agent in any repository:

1. What did the agent do (normalized trace)?
2. Was it correct (ground-truth annotation, possibly AI-assisted)?
3. What kind of failure was it (versioned failure taxonomy)?
4. Will this fail again tomorrow (executable regression + dataset)?
5. Is anyone shipping a release that prevents or detects it (signed evidence)?

## Business value

The Intent Solutions stack — Intent Eval Platform (IEP), Bob's Big Brain (BBB),
AGP, JRig, rollout-gate, Evidence Bench, Mission Control — already evaluates
agents in narrow lanes. Without a unified trace-to-decision loop, evaluation
effort is wasted: signals are duplicated, taxonomies drift, datasets rot,
regressions are re-built instead of recycled, and rollout decisions are made
on partial evidence. The program converts scattered evaluation work into a
self-reinforcing learning loop that compounds quality with every accepted
annotation.

## Problem statement

- Agent traces are produced in multiple incompatible shapes (claude-code,
  JRig, IEP, third-party OTel, vendor SDKs) and have no normalized form.
- Annotation exists ad-hoc inside individual repos; there is no shared
  annotation backbone, no human-approval audit log, and no AI-proposal
  workflow.
- Failure taxonomies are repo-local, undocumented, and version-controlled
  by accident.
- Evaluation datasets are not versioned, not reproducible, and not lineage-
  traceable to the annotations that produced them.
- Regression suites are hand-curated, not generated from accepted findings.
- Evidence receipts are repo-local and inconsistent, blocking the
  rollout-gate from enforcing at the estate level.
- Mission Control cannot project evaluation outcomes, dataset freshness,
  taxonomy drift, or evidence validity across repos.

## Desired end state

A single production system that, end-to-end, can:

- Ingest agent traces from any source into a normalized, content-hashed store.
- Cluster traces by semantic similarity with deterministic quality checks.
- Sample traces for human annotation using uncertainty + coverage strategies.
- Allow AI to propose labels but require human acceptance to mutate
  canonical state.
- Version the failure taxonomy with migration rules.
- Version the evaluation datasets with lineage to the annotations that built
  them.
- Generate executable regression cases from accepted findings.
- Run the regressions against JRig and produce gate decisions.
- Produce signed evidence receipts consumed by Evidence Bench.
- Project coverage, drift, and risk into Mission Control for every
  repository and agent.
- Ingest accepted failure patterns into BBB as cited institutional memory.
- Enforce permissions and policy via AGP at every step.

## Scope

In scope:

- Audit both GitHub estates (jeremylongshore + intent-solutions-io).
- Inventory, classify, and reconcile every existing evaluation, trace,
  annotation, evidence, and rollout-gate component.
- Vendor-neutral research across open-source and commercial options for
  every subsystem.
- Design of contracts (schemas) for normalized traces, clusters,
  annotations, taxonomies, datasets, regressions, evals, evidence, and
  projections.
- Implementation of the subsystems owned by IEP, JRig, rollout-gate,
  Evidence Bench, AGP, BBB, and Mission Control.
- Pilot on one controlled agent + repo before broader rollout.
- Documentation, runbooks, and the final program AAR.

Out of scope:

- Architecture or tool-selection decisions made today. Both require future
  research (Group B).
- Replacing individual repo-local evaluation scripts until a replacement
  proof exists (J12, E8).
- Moving application source code into intent-os.
- Production adoption of any new system without owner sign-off (J14).
- Any change to GitHub ownership, Beads/Dolt ownership, Plane ownership,
  or BBB authority semantics.

## Non-goals

- No monolithic new repository. The program lives across existing
  repositories and adds one IEP-owned capability repository only if the
  architecture requires it (C17, E1).
- No AI-promoted labels that bypass human approval. AI may propose,
  humans approve.
- No "just use the vendor SDK" short-cuts. Contracts are the source of
  truth; SDKs adapt to them, not the reverse.
- No lock-in to a specific clustering algorithm, embedding model,
  annotation UI, or signed-evidence format until research selects one.

## Platform ownership boundaries (planned; future research must verify)

- **Intent Eval Platform (IEP)** owns evaluation logic, trace analysis,
  datasets, taxonomies, scoring, and evidence generation.
- **Intent OS / Mission Control** owns portfolio visibility, ownership,
  status, governance, work correlation, and projections. Does NOT own
  evaluation logic.
- **Bob's Big Brain (BBB)** owns governed institutional knowledge;
  accepts ONLY human-approved, evidence-backed findings as memory.
- **AGP** owns agent authority and policy enforcement; sits between every
  subsystem that touches a trace or annotation and the data plane.
- **JRig** owns the binary-skill evaluation harness; consumes IEP
  datasets and emits evidence receipts.
- **rollout-gate** owns the merge-blocking decision; consumes evidence
  receipts and gate-result/v1 predicates.
- **Evidence Bench** owns signed evidence storage and verification.
- **Plane** is a human coordination projection only; never authoritative.
- **Beads/Dolt** owns canonical work state and dependency state.
- **GitHub** owns commits, branches, PRs, reviews, and merge history.
- **Individual repos** own their code and repo-local tests.

## Relationship to Mission Control

Mission Control surfaces this program through:

- Coverage projections (which repos have trace ingestion, which don't).
- Annotation throughput projections (accepted vs rejected per agent/repo).
- Taxonomy drift projections (which repos use the current version).
- Dataset freshness projections (age of latest evaluation dataset).
- Evidence validity projections (valid/invalid signatures per repo).
- Readiness + risk views used for owner production-adoption decisions.

## Relationship to Intent Eval Platform (IEP)

IEP is the technical owner of:

- The normalized trace contract (C1).
- Clustering + sampling pipelines (C3, C8, D6, D15).
- Annotation storage + audit log (D8, D10).
- Failure taxonomy registry + versioning (D13, D14).
- Dataset builder + versioning (D17, D18).
- Regression-case generator (D19).
- Evaluation runners (D20).
- Signed evidence producer (D21).
- Access controls for sensitive traces (D22).

IEP ships the capability as an addition to its estate, not a fork.

## Relationship to JRig

JRig consumes IEP-produced datasets + regression cases, executes them
against binary skills, and emits evidence receipts. JRig's existing
SkillVersion entity + signed evidence reports
(`bd_000-projects-0r8m`) are the technical ancestor of this program's
regression + evidence contracts (D19, D21). JRig does NOT own the
taxonomy or the dataset — IEP does. JRig owns execution + evidence
emission.

## Relationship to rollout-gate

rollout-gate consumes evidence receipts and gate-result/v1 predicates
from JRig. Existing rollout-gate lanes
(`bd_000-projects-444u`, `bd_000-projects-1332`, `bd_000-projects-apzn.5`)
are added to, not replaced by, this program's projections. rollout-gate
does NOT own taxonomy or evidence; it owns merge-block decisions.

## Relationship to Evidence Bench

Evidence Bench stores and verifies signed evidence receipts produced by
IEP + JRig. The program does NOT introduce a second evidence store;
it consolidates onto Evidence Bench. Deferred Evidence Bundle signature
verification (`bd_000-projects-h08j.7`) becomes unblocked by this program.

## Relationship to Bob's Big Brain (BBB)

BBB accepts ONLY:

- Accepted (human-approved) failure patterns (G2).
- Cited evidence receipts (G4).
- Expiry + supersession + correction rules (G5).
BBB rejects (does NOT promote):

- AI-proposed annotations without human acceptance (G3).
- Repo-local opinions not backed by an evidence receipt.

## Relationship to AGP

AGP enforces:

- Trace access permissions (H1).
- Reviewer + annotator permissions (H2).
- AI-proposal permissions (H3).
- Authority required for taxonomy mutation (H4).
- Authority required for eval generation/promotion (H5).
- Fail-closed behavior for missing/invalid policy (H6).
- Policy decisions embedded in evidence receipts (H7).

## Repository-estate audit requirement

A formal current-state audit (A1-A8) is the entry gate for any
architecture work. The audit must classify every relevant component as:

- existing and sufficient
- existing but incomplete
- requires upgrade
- duplicate
- stale
- missing
- ownership unclear
- owner decision required

Classification must be evidence-based (commit history, code references,
test artifacts, release tags), not repository-name based.

## Human-approval requirement

- AI may propose annotations and taxonomy changes.
- Humans approve ground truth.
- No annotation or taxonomy mutation enters canonical state without a
  human-reviewer identity attached (C5, H4).

## Deterministic-first requirement

- All clustering, sampling, evaluation, and evidence steps MUST be
  reproducible given the same inputs and policy state (C1-C13, D6, D18,
  D21).
- Non-deterministic components (e.g., AI proposals) MUST be auditable
  (the model, the prompt, the seed if any) and MUST NOT affect canonical
  state without human acceptance (H1-H6).

## Vendor-neutral requirement

- No vendor lock-in at the contract level. Tools and SDKs are chosen
  later (Group B).
- Contracts are open schemas (JSON Schema with version fields).
- Switching vendors MUST NOT require schema migration.

## Evidence and reproducibility requirements

- Every evaluation run produces a signed evidence receipt (C13, D21).
- Every dataset version is reproducible from its declared inputs
  (C9, D18).
- Every regression suite is reproducible from its declared inputs
  (C10, D19).
- Every evidence receipt carries the policy version it was evaluated
  against (H7).

## Security and privacy considerations

- Traces may contain user prompt text, secrets, and PII by accident.
  The program MUST NOT promote trace content into BBB or any other
  shared store until D22 (access + sensitive-data controls) ships.
- AGP enforcement is required at every trace access point (H1).
- Deletion must be supported and audited (C19).
- The owner-decision gate on production adoption (J14) MUST include
  a security + privacy review (J12) before any promotion.

## Deployment-placement questions (to be answered by future research)

- Does the normalized trace store live in IEP, in intent-os, or in a new
  repository? (C17, E1).
- Does the annotation backend live in IEP or in BBB? (C17).
- Does the failure-taxonomy registry live in IEP, in intent-os, or in
  Evidence Bench? (C17).
- Does the dataset store live in IEP or in Evidence Bench? (C17).
- Does the signed-evidence producer run as a library, a service, or a
  GH Action? (C18).
- Does Mission Control consume the projection APIs via pull, push, or
  webhook? (C14).

## Major risks

1. **Architectural lock-in** if contracts are chosen before research.
   Mitigation: B12 produces build-vs-adopt recommendations BEFORE C1-C19.
2. **AI label leakage** if proposals can mutate canonical state. Mitigation:
   G3 + H4 enforce human gate.
3. **Sensitive trace leakage** into BBB or evidence receipts. Mitigation:
   D22 + H1 + J12.
4. **Duplicate data planes** if Mission Control builds its own evaluation
   logic. Mitigation: C14 contracts reference IEP-owned projection APIs.
5. **Dataset rot** if versioning is not version-controlled from day 1.
   Mitigation: C9 + D18 enforce reproducibility from inputs.
6. **Rollout-gate flapping** if evidence validity is fragile. Mitigation:
   C13 + J12 + J13.
7. **Estate audit gap** if A1-A8 are skipped. Mitigation: C20 cannot ship
   without A8 sign-off.

## Owner decisions expected

- Architecture placement (C17): IEP, intent-os, new repo.
- Annotation backend placement (C17).
- Failure-taxonomy storage placement (C17).
- Dataset storage placement (C17).
- Policy version numbering scheme (H4).
- Evidence signature algorithm + key custodian (C13).
- Pilot agent + repo selection (J1).
- Production adoption gate criteria (J14).

## Completion definition

All three of:

1. The audit (A8) has been signed off by the owner and reconciled
   against Mission Control's estate graph.
2. The architecture (C20) has been ratified via the ADR set and the
   owner has signed the placement decisions (C17).
3. The pilot (J3-J10) has produced a signed evidence package covering
   one controlled agent + one repo, and the owner has approved
   production adoption (J14).

The first seven consecutive days of production traces ingested, clustered,
sampled, annotated, accepted by humans, and projected into Mission Control
without policy violation is the hard acceptance bar (analogous to the
"7 consecutive nights" rule for the MiniMax migration, `bd_000-projects-slfo`).

## Child-bead index

- **Group A — Estate audit and current-state discovery**
  A1 Audit `jeremylongshore` GitHub repos
  A2 Audit `intent-solutions-io` GitHub repos
  A3 Build the evaluation-capability inventory
  A4 Map repository and package dependencies
  A5 Identify canonical, duplicate, stale, experimental components
  A6 Produce the gap and upgrade register
  A7 Reconcile the audit with Mission Control registry and estate graph
  A8 Current-state audit report and owner review

- **Group B — External research and build-vs-adopt analysis**
  B1-B10 Research beads (trace collection, clustering, annotation,
       sampling, AI proposals, taxonomy, datasets, evals, evidence,
       privacy)
  B11 Competitor + open-source comparison
  B12 Build-vs-adopt recommendation

- **Group C — Architecture and contract design**
  C1-C19 Individual contract beads
  C20 Final architecture ADR set

- **Group D — Foundational implementation plan**
  D1-D22 Implementation beads (trace ingestion through access controls)

- **Group E — Intent Eval Platform integration**
  E1-E9 IEP integration beads

- **Group F — Mission Control and estate governance**
  F1-F13 Mission Control projection beads

- **Group G — Bob's Big Brain and organizational learning**
  G1-G6 BBB ingestion beads

- **Group H — AGP and governed agent operation**
  H1-H7 AGP policy beads

- **Group I — Testing and validation**
  I1-I15 Testing plan beads

- **Group J — Pilot, rollout, and adoption**
  J1-J16 Pilot + rollout beads

- **Group K — Documentation, runbooks, and handoff**
  K1-K15 Documentation beads

## High-level dependency sequence

1. A1 + A2 (parallel) → A3 → A4 + A5 → A6 → A7 → A8 (entry gates).
2. B1-B10 (parallel after A8) → B11 → B12.
3. C1-C19 (parallel after B12 + A8) → C20.
4. D1-D22 (sequenced by data flow: ingest → store → cluster → sample
   → annotate → AI proposals → human acceptance → taxonomy → datasets →
   regression → evals → evidence → access controls).
5. E1-E9 (sequenced after their corresponding D-beads).
6. F1-F7 (after projection contracts) → F8-F11 → F12 → F13.
7. G1 (after C15) → G2-G6.
8. H1-H6 (after C16 + C19) → H7.
9. I1-I15 (each paired with its target bead).
10. J1-J5 (pilot) → J6-J10 (first artifacts) → J11-J13 (reviews) → J14
    (production gate) → J15-J16 (expansion).
11. K1-K15 (parallel with their corresponding implementation beads).
design: No monolithic new repository. IEP-owned capability additions only where C17 placement decisions require. Tool selection deferred to Group B research. AI proposals never mutate canonical state without human acceptance (G3 + H4).
acceptance_criteria: Three things true at the same time: (1) audit bead A8 has been owner-signed-off AND reconciled against Mission Control's estate graph AND a corresponding Mission Control readiness+risk view exists in F12; (2) architecture ADR set C20 is ratified AND the owner has signed the placement decisions in C17; (3) pilot beads J3-J10 have produced a signed evidence package covering exactly one controlled agent + one repo, AND the owner has approved production adoption via J14. Hard acceptance bar: 7 consecutive production days with trace ingestion + clustering + sampling + annotation + human acceptance + Mission Control projection, with zero policy violations and zero unreviewed AI proposals promoting to canonical state.
notes:
