title: Refactor prescreen gate to split pull_request from pull_request_target so fork PRs don't need allow-unsafe-pr-checkout
description:
## Why

CCP's pr-prescreen.yml runs on pull_request_target so it can post trusted comments using base-repo secrets (DEPLOY_KEY etc.). It also checks out the PR's HEAD to run a validator. Under actions/checkout@v6 (and v7), checking out fork PR code from a pull_request_target workflow is blocked by default; the opt-out is allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true, which GitHub explicitly named loud because it enables a known pwn-request pattern (Nx, PostHog, TanStack were compromised this way in 2025–2026). The current fork-safe design (validator copied from base, never executes PR code) is correct, but it's a per-future-maintainer invariant. We want the safety in workflow architecture, not in code-review diligence.

## What ships

Two jobs in .github/workflows/pr-prescreen.yml:
- Job A (pull_request): runs the validator on the PR's code in fork context. No secrets exposed. Reads the diff, computes verdicts.
- Job B (pull_request_target): posts the trusted comment back using base-repo GITHUB_TOKEN. Reads only the diff JSON produced by Job A (uploaded as an artifact). Never checks out PR code.

Both jobs together preserve the existing behavior of "a fork PR gets an automatic prescreen comment with validator output" without ever checking out fork code under pull_request_target.

## How

- Move validator run to a new job triggered on pull_request.
- Validator output uploaded as an artifact from Job A.
- Job B (pull_request_target) downloads the artifact and posts the comment. No checkout of the PR's HEAD in Job B.
- Update 000-docs/265-DR-GUID-pr-prescreen-system.md to document the new shape and remove the invariant language about "never executes PR code" (now structural, not policy).

## Acceptance

- A fork PR (e.g. #1105 UIZZE submission) gets a prescreen comment posted by the workflow.
- Job B never executes actions/checkout with ref pointing at the PR's HEAD/merge commit.
- The fork-safe-design invariant becomes structural (the workflow physically cannot check out fork code under pull_request_target).
- Existing required CI checks on CCP remain unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Switching prescreen trigger to pull_request only (different product behavior — loses trusted commenting).
- Skipping prescreen on fork PRs entirely (Option 2; cheaper but loses automatic fork-PR review).
- The UIZZE PR (#1105) is unblocked by this PR landing, but should not be bundled into it.
- Bead refiner-lab (intent-eval-lab) -- this is CCP-only.

## Refs

- GitHub: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target
- actions/checkout release notes: v7 (June 2026) blocks unsafe fork-PR checkouts by default; v6 backport in July 2026.
- Orca Security Pull Request Nightmare writeup (2025-09-24): real-world pwn-request compromises at Google, Microsoft, Fortune-500.
- Internal: 000-docs/265-DR-GUID-pr-prescreen-system.md describes the current fork-safe design and its read-not-execute invariant.
acceptance_criteria: Refactor is done when a fork PR gets a prescreen comment posted AND no job under pull_request_target runs actions/checkout with ref pointing at the PR's HEAD or merge commit. Verified by rerunning prescreen against a fork PR (e.g. #1105) and reviewing the actions log.
close_reason: Merged as PR #1126 (commit 862ab3a) on 2026-07-24. Two-job prescreen refactor + DeepSeek→MiniMax vendor swap both shipped. Live CI confirmed: prescreen/validate and prescreen/respond both pass against the merged workflow. PR #1105 (UIZZE) was auto-closed by the 'Closes #1105' merge body — reopened in OPEN state so the contributor can re-trigger prescreen by pushing a no-op (or closing/reopening will work once they push). Required CI on the merge commit: 21 SUCCESS / 1 SKIPPED (trufflehog, unrelated) / 1 CANCELLED (legacy 'prescreen' job superseded by prescreen/validate + prescreen/respond, both SUCCESS).

description: FF#2 covers exactly one contract - skill-frontmatter, via a regex written against the agentskills.io frontmatter table, with cmd_check hardcoding agentskills-spec-v1.0.md. agentskills-spec is one of the 5 sources that did NOT drift. This is the difference between a semantic gate that is blind and one that is narrow. The pieces already exist: scripts/extract-{agent-definition,hook-config,marketplace-catalog,mcp,plugin-manifest}-projection.py plus a committed projection.json + PROVENANCE.md + vendor-meta.json per surface under specs/_vendor/upstream/. Coverage after wiring is 6 of 16 - say so EXPLICITLY: the rest are release feeds and changelogs with no normative field shape, legitimately byte-hash-only, and that must be recorded in the registry so nobody later mistakes 'no extractor' for 'not covered by design'. Do not treat byte-hash as a substitute for a projection on a surface that has one. Findings: (1) all five extract-*-projection.py already have --extract/--write/--check/--self-test/--vendor-dir, so wiring looks trivial. (2) It is NOT: all five --check read specs/_vendor/upstream/<contract>/, the HAND-VENDORED deep-capture tree, which fetch-capture.py cannot write ('upstream' is not a surface id) and whose vendor-meta is stamped 2026-06-12. Point every Intent Eval Platform repo at every Bob's Big Brain surface: real seed data, A/B arms, signed evidence, and a public scoreboard row per repo. Advisory first; enforcing only after the doc-110 graduation criteria are met.

BASELINE (verified 2026-07-22): zero of BBB's 5 SKILL.md files, 4 agents, and 1 MCP server had ever been behaviorally evaluated. Only the registrar emitted a signed evidence row; the other three repos were dark.

Wave 1 — SCAFFOLDED, BLOCKED (jeremylongshore/intent-eval-lab#230):
  bbb-seed-v1 machinery built and verified; corpus deliberately EMPTY. Blocking finding: all
  17,321 brain memories are classified sensitivity=internal and none are public, so any public
  corpus is a decision to publish internally-classified content. Needs operator sign-off.

Waves 2-5 — NOT STARTED: j-rig behavioral eval-specs + BBB roster; the four A/B axes;
advisory rollout-gate lanes in all four repos; graduation to enforcing.

Sibling of the five 2026-07-16 dogfood epics (184o, sbs7, thi7, 7dnu, awuw). Wave 0's dashboard
pin fix is arguably a sbs7 follow-up.
notes:
Drift-fix wave COMPLETE 2026-07-22, all CI green. THREE PRs: (1) bobs-big-brain-compiler#182 [22/0] — kernel pin ^0.1.1 -> ^0.10.0 (caret on a 0.x major caps at 0.1.x so it could NEVER reach 0.10.0; 9 minor versions of drift) PLUS the bigger find: buildAndValidateEvidenceBundle was FAIL-OPEN — if neither kernel schema export resolved it returned an UNVALIDATED bundle silently, and the trigger for that path is precisely a version mismatch, i.e. the state the repo was already in. Now throws; 2 regression tests added, mutation-checked (reverting the guard makes the test fail). NOTE kernel-shadow-check reports this repo CLEAN — it only detects re-declared kernel types, so it is blind to stale-range drift. (2) bobs-big-brain-registrar#315 [15/0] — deleted the DEAD vendored audit-harness v0.1.0 tree + wrapper; nothing invoked it (CI uses the local scripts/harness-pin.sh), so upgrading would just be newer dead code. Documented that the local harness-pin.sh fork can now retire because v1.3.0 added .harness-hash-extra-patterns, the exact configurability its header says didn't exist — deliberately NOT bundled (changes the gate on every policy artifact; manifest formats unproven compatible). (3) intent-audit-harness#132 [32/0] — installer defaulted to a hardcoded v1.1.5 (stale, and missing kernel-shadow-check.sh) AND its own documented pin form put the env var on curl not bash so it never reached the script. Now resolves latest release with a fallback floor, adds pipe-safe --version, prints the resolution source so a missed pin is visible. Likely root cause of the registrar's v0.1.0 tree. My install.sh edit tripped the repo's own HARNESS_TAMPERED pin (all 6 CI failures were that ONE root cause) — re-pinned as designed.
Detector blind spot FIXED — intent-audit-harness#133 [32/0 CI green]. Jeremy pushed back on my noting-but-not-fixing that kernel-shadow-check was blind to stale ranges. Root issue: the script's OWN header states the harm ('validate against its own stale copy instead of the kernel the dashboard verifies with') but it only detected re-DECLARED types. A stale dependency range causes the identical outcome and was invisible — it reported bobs-big-brain-compiler CLEAN while that repo sat at ^0.1.1 vs a 0.10.0 kernel. Added a third detection class (range-currency) to the SAME detector rather than a new script, because it's the same harm and a separate tool is one more thing nobody wires in. Narrow parser: caret/tilde/exact/open/workspace evaluated; compound/hyphen/wildcard report UNKNOWN and surface for a human — chosen because half-parsing returns a confident WRONG answer (my first draft called '0.1.x || ^0.2.0' stale purely because of the leading digit; the new test caught it). Unresolvable kernel version SKIPS loudly and withholds the clean claim. Added the detector's FIRST test suite: 22 cases, deterministic+offline via KERNEL_LATEST_VERSION, incl. a no-regression case for the original class. Verified against real repos: compiler@origin/main -> 1 stale range flagged (the bug it used to miss), compiler@fix -> clean, registrar -> clean, self -> clean, --strict exits 1. Stays ADVISORY. Editing the script tripped the repo's own HARNESS_TAMPERED pin; re-pinned as designed.
COURSE CORRECTION 2026-07-22 — intent-audit-harness#133 WITHDRAWN, and the finding recorded in the note above it is RETRACTED.

The prior note claimed a 'detector blind spot' — that kernel-shadow-check was blind to stale dependency ranges — and shipped a third detection class to close it. That framing contradicts ratified platform architecture. DR-064 § 3 rule (a) FORWARD compatibility exists precisely so a consumer does NOT have to be current ('the load-bearing rule for incremental kernel releases'), and Blueprint B § 7.0.1 names the coordinated cross-repo deploy as 'the exact failure mode that independent package versioning exists to prevent.' Consumers lagging the kernel is the DESIGN, not drift. Run estate-wide the currency class flagged six repos — j-rig-binary-eval x4, intent-eval-dashboard, intent-rollout-gate, claude-code-plugins, intent-eval-lab, bobs-big-brain-compiler — every one of them conformant. A gate that fails ratified-correct configurations trains people to ignore the lane, and contradicting a ratified DR is an ISEDC path, not a PR.

Could not substantiate the harm either. On the exact subpath the compiler imports (@intentsolutions/core/validators/v1): 0.1.1 DOES export EvidenceBundleSchema (65 exports) and so does 0.10.0 (165). Required-field sets are IDENTICAL across the two — 11 fields, unchanged; the only delta in nine minor versions is one OPTIONAL field, pre_registration_hash. That is a textbook Blueprint B § 7.0.1 Expand phase. The compiler's 17 pre-existing evidence-bundle tests pass unchanged under 0.10.0.

Two claims in the prior notes are wrong and are corrected here: (1) 'j-rig has three files defining kernel-owned types' — FALSE. Five of the six flagged lines are 'type X,' entries inside 'export { ... } from "@intentsolutions/core/..."' blocks, i.e. RE-EXPORTS, the single-source-of-truth pattern the detector exists to encourage. The sixth (packages/core/src/schemas/evidence-bundle.ts:192) is a local alias over the kernel's own imported schema. (2) The class I called 'the one that already worked' is the one carrying the bug.

REPLACEMENT WORK — intent-audit-harness#134: the real defect is that the detector cries wolf on correct code and had no tests. Class 2 now anchors on declaration syntax (=, {, <, (, :, extends, implements) instead of the bare keyword; class 1 exempts x-redirect stubs (the ratified Blueprint B § 7.0 / DR-018 § 6.4 alpha-minus pattern the lab's own schema-drift.yml already allowlists); dist/ and build/ join the path allowlist. 27 contract tests added, offline+deterministic, wired into CI AHEAD of the detector. Verified: j-rig 3 findings -> 1, lab 1 -> 0, dashboard/rollout-gate/self clean and unchanged, mutation check still exits 1 under --strict, shellcheck clean, semver 31/31, regression 17/17, escape-scan 0/0/0, .harness-hash re-pinned.

RECORDED: intent-eval-lab#231 lands 000-docs/111-AT-SPEC-kernel-version-skew-is-by-design-2026-07-22.md — the scope record so this is not re-derived. It also names the LEGITIMATE version of the currency idea: Blueprint B § 7.0.1 phase 2's producer-time deprecation warning against 'producers pinned to the pre-field kernel' — the KERNEL's job, at producer time, scoped to one field mid-migration and tied to the deprecation registry. Not a blanket CI gate. Not currently scheduled.

STANDING: wiring kernel-shadow-check into more repos stays DEFERRED until #134 lands — propagating a crying-wolf detector is worse than not propagating it. Also note the detector is consumer-side: running it inside intent-eval-core flags the kernel for being the kernel, so any propagation excludes the kernel repo. Waves 2-5 (behavioral eval-specs, BBB roster, A/B axes, rollout-gate lanes) are untouched by this correction and remain open under this epic.

title: Postmortem: the IEP spec-currency auto-update loop silently went stale — document root cause + the L1/L2 fixes shipped + remaining follow-ups
description:
WHY THINGS GOT OUT OF DATE (root cause, 2026-06-28). The spec-drift-watch (intent-eval-lab, daily 09:00 UTC, 16 upstream surfaces, FF#2 field-diff, feeding the kernel SSoT) LOOKED alive (green checks) but the auto-currency loop was broken in THREE places, all silent:

1. PERSISTENCE (L1) — the watcher fetched + field-diffed all 16 surfaces but EVERY commit-back push FAILED main's 9 required status checks (the github-actions bot is not an admin; enforce_admins:false). So the kernel SSoT snapshots, the liveness .state.json, lineage, and currency evidence NEVER persisted — committed state frozen at the last MANUAL capture PR. .state.json stayed last_run_utc:null forever -> watcher-liveness.py printed 'bootstrap (OK)' every run -> dead-man heartbeat INERT -> dashboard read DEGRADED while the watcher was 'green'. The guard built to 'never fail silent-green' WAS silent-green.

2. INSTALL DRIFT — CCPI pinned @intentsolutions/core 0.9.0 (authoring/v2, current) but node_modules had a stale 0.4.1 (authoring/v1 only). Consumers read the stale v1.

3. CONSUMPTION (L2) — CCPI's PLUGIN_JSON_FIELDS was hand-maintained with NO comparison to the kernel. Even when the kernel SSoT was current, CCPI didn't consume it -> went stale silently -> required hand-patches (CCPI schema 3.12.0).

FIXES SHIPPED 2026-06-28:
- L1: intent-eval-lab#207 — spec-drift-watch checkout uses an admin-bypass push token (SPEC_DRIFT_PUSH_TOKEN) + a durable-liveness commit-back step. VERIFIED on main: bot commit-backs land, .state.json last_run_utc advances (was null), 16 surfaces tracked, DEGRADED clears.
- Install drift: pnpm install reconciled CCPI to 0.9.0.
- L2: CCPI schema 3.14.0 — load_kernel_plugin_fields() + a plugin_manifest block in kernel_shadow_report(); PLUGIN_JSON_FIELDS now drift-gated against authoring/v2 via the kernel-shadow CI lane. Caught + adopted a metadata field on first run (fields_match:true).

FULL WRITE-UP: claude-code-plugins 000-docs/692-AA-AACR-spec-currency-audit-2026-06-28.md (§ 0.5 is the root cause).

REMAINING FOLLOW-UPS (this bead tracks):
a. lab->kernel RELEASE cadence: the drift-watch keeps the lab _vendor current, but promoting that into a published @intentsolutions/core release (so CCPI's pin sees it) is still manual. Automate or schedule.
b. SPEC_DRIFT_PUSH_TOKEN is currently Jeremy's broad gh token (works; accepted tradeoff). Optionally tighten to a scoped fine-grained PAT later.
c. metadata plugin.json field: adopted into CCPI to match kernel; confirm it is a real/intended field vs a kernel-overlay artifact.
d. daily cross-reference routine (watch-the-watchers) to verify all umbrella layers actually execute + stay consistent — being set up.
e. L2 for the OTHER hand-maintained sets (SKILL/agent shadows exist; ensure they're all gated). Related: SAK epic bd_000-projects-9k5h.

title: Make audit-harness CLI emit-evidence emit kernel-valid gate-result/v1 predicate bodies
description: DISCOVERED by the beads-dolt dogfood (first IEP external-adopter convergence run, 2026-06-19). The CLI-exposed 'audit-harness emit-evidence' (scripts/emit-evidence.sh) wraps gate-result rows into an in-toto Statement with predicateType https://evals.intentsolutions.io/gate-result/v1 but the predicate BODY is the legacy draft envelope (gate_id/result/policy_hash/input_hash/timestamp/runner/commit_sha/metadata). This breaks the audit-harness→kernel→rollout-gate convergence (DR-010 Q3 unification thesis: every validator emits a kernel-valid Evidence Bundle). Verify: conform | emit-evidence → GateResultV1Schema.safeParse passes → rollout-gate accepts. Evidence: ~/000-projects/beads-dolt/DOGFOOD.md Finding 1.

Gemini review hardening (semver-degrade + coverage both-keys) addressed. title: Eval the eval set: coverage / leakage / calibration / adversarial-pass-rate metrics in Phase A (Karpathy F-AK-005 binding)
description:
**Plan reference:** DR-028 implementation + Karpathy F-AK-005 P1 ("no eval of the eval set itself").

**Scope:** Phase A produces eval-set quality metrics: coverage, leakage, calibration, adversarial-pass-rate. The Refiner's verdicts are only as good as the eval set; the eval set's quality needs its own measurement layer.

**Metrics shipped in Phase A:**
- Coverage: stratified-sampling completeness across declared skill capabilities
- Leakage: detection of train/eval contamination (refiner has seen eval items)
- Calibration: are pass/fail thresholds well-calibrated to actual skill behavior?
- Adversarial-pass-rate: synthetic adversarial examples; what % do skills pass that they should fail?

**Per SkillsBench 16/84 (~19%) regression rate (DR-028 P0-RATIFY-1):** adversarial-pass-rate dimension is required to detect the regression patterns SkillsBench documented.

**Architectural commitments honored:** AC-3 (multi-dim ScoreRecord — adversarial_pass_rate is one of the dimensions).

**Coordination:** parent = bd_000-projects-214c.

**Bandwidth budget per 029-DR-BAND:** 1.0 FTE-day (folded into Phase A bootstrap work).

title: Implement Hook hook (L3) — PostToolUse:Bash on git commit/push matcher runs agentic gate against rejected-edit buffer + shadow-validation ($$ Opus, rate-limited)
description:
L3 of Pre-Trip. Sets the catch — the most expensive + thorough gate.

Hook event: PostToolUse:Bash (matcher: command starts with 'git commit' OR 'git push'). Logic:
1. Run 'git diff --staged' to get the staged changes
2. If no SKILL.md modified: pass through
3. If SKILL.md modified: invoke agentic gate
   a. Read the SKILL.md diff + surrounding skills/ directory context
   b. Check the proposed edit against .j-rig/keeper/log.jsonl rejected-edit buffer (was this edit pattern already tried + rejected on this skill or similar?)
   c. Optional shadow-validation: score the proposed edit against held-out eval set; report delta
   d. Surface findings to Claude as a turn-3 context message
4. Rate-limit: max 1 Opus invocation per N minutes per repo to control cost

Cost: $$ tier — Opus for the agentic gate. Rate-limited per security-guidance reference pattern.

Hook script: plugins/productivity/j-rig/hooks/hook.sh.

Plan ref: § 3 commitment #8, § 4 Phase B Pre-Trip table.

title: Implement Line hook (L2) — Stop hook captures end-of-turn rollouts; fires Refiner in background after N rollouts on a skill ($ Sonnet+Haiku)
description:
L2 of Pre-Trip. The line tells you the bite is real.

Hook event: Stop (end of agent turn). Logic:
1. Check if a skill was invoked during the turn (via tool-call trace)
2. If yes AND j-rig Binary Eval has scored the rollout: append to .j-rig/keeper/log.jsonl
3. Count rollouts on this skill since last optimizer pass
4. If >= threshold N (default 10): fire Keeper proposer in background via 'j-rig keeper propose <skill>' (Sonnet default per § 3 #5)
5. If a candidate is produced: surface it in next-turn context so Claude can see + offer to /j-rig promote

Cost: $ tier — Sonnet for the proposer, Haiku for the scoring (delegated). Hard budget cap from sibling Keeper task.

Hook script: plugins/productivity/j-rig/hooks/line.sh.

Plan ref: § 3 commitment #8, § 4 Phase B Pre-Trip table.

title: Build Skill Refiner CLI (5 commands: bootstrap, score, propose, apply, status) in @j-rig/refiner/bin/
description:
Thin CLI wrapper over the library API. 5 commands, all delegating to the value-oriented functions:

- j-rig keeper bootstrap <skill> [--from-rollouts] [--golden <path>]
- j-rig keeper score <skill> --eval-set <hash-or-path> [--model haiku|sonnet|opus]
- j-rig keeper propose <skill> [--from-rollouts <hash>] [--optimizer sonnet|opus]
- j-rig keeper apply <proposal-hash>
- j-rig keeper status <skill> [--show-rejected]

All commands operate on values: take hashes/paths, emit hashes/paths. No mutable state in the CLI itself; all persistence goes through the storage layer (sibling task).

CLI surface stays minimal — the plugin in Epic 2 will wrap these with hook-driven invocations, NOT add new functionality.

title: Implement append-only event log (.j-rig/refiner/log.jsonl) + content-addressed store (.j-rig/refiner/store/<hash>) + best-pointer (.j-rig/refiner/pointers/<skill>/best)
description:
The persistence layer for Keeper. Per § 3 commitment #2: append-only event log; never in-place SKILL.md mutation.

Three storage primitives:
1. .j-rig/keeper/log.jsonl — append-only event log. Each line: timestamped value-record (eval_set_bootstrapped, score_computed, edit_proposed, edit_applied, edit_accepted, edit_rejected, promoted).
2. .j-rig/keeper/store/<hash> — content-addressed value store. Each SkillVersion, EditProposal, ScoreRecord persists as immutable value file keyed by its sha256.
3. .j-rig/keeper/pointers/<skill>/best — single mutable pointer file (just a hash string). 'Current best' is a pointer, not a destructive mutation.

This layer is what enables: replay of any optimization history, audit-trail reconstruction, drift detection vs prior versions, supersession-tracking. It also satisfies the policy that bd_000-projects-uprg ratifies (forward-compat for immutable artifact semantics).

Plan ref: § 3 commitment #2, § 4 Phase A.

title: Implement Skill Refiner apply() + accept() — pure SkillDoc→SkillDocV2 transformation and strict-improvement gate over multi-dim ScoreRecord
description:
Two functions, one task because they're the acceptance discipline together.

apply(skillDoc, edit) → SkillDocV2. Pure transformation. No I/O. Takes EditProposal ops + applies them in declared order. Output is content-addressed (new SkillDocHash) so the chain is reproducible.

accept(scoreV1, scoreV2) → boolean. Strict-improvement gate. STRICT meaning: no dimension regresses AND at least one dimension improves AND the primary (behavioral) dimension improves by > delta-threshold. Anti-Goodhart per § 3 commitment #3 — accept does NOT pick a winner by averaging dimensions; it requires the proposal to NOT make anything worse.

The acceptance gate is the durable contribution per § 3 commitment #7. When frontier-native optimizers arrive, the harness + gate stay; only propose() gets swapped.

Plan ref: § 3 commitments #2/#3/#7, § 4 Phase A.

- Sigstore provenance attestation EXISTS in public Rekor (logIndex=1631712090) — pointing at a tarball that was never published. This is an irreversible-on-Rekor footprint but harmless (no consumer can fetch the tarball, the attestation just points at a publish that didn't complete).
- npm registry still has @intentsolutions/core@0.1.0 as latest (from 2026-05-17)
- package.json on main says 0.1.1

Why v0.1.0 worked (2026-05-17) but v0.1.1 didn't (2026-05-26, 8 days later):
- Most likely: NPM_TOKEN expired (npm automation tokens typically 90d-1yr; could be a shorter policy)
- Alternative: npm 2FA requirement changed at @intentsolutions org level requiring automation-2FA token
- Less likely: package access was modified at org level

Fix action (user-side, not Claude-side):
1. npm login → npm token create --read-only=false --cidr-whitelist=<...> (or use granular token in npm UI)
2. Update GitHub Actions secret NPM_TOKEN in jeremylongshore/intent-eval-core repo settings
3. Re-trigger publish: gh workflow run release.yml --ref v0.1.1 (if workflow supports manual dispatch on tag) OR delete + recreate tag: git push origin :v0.1.1 && git tag -fa v0.1.1 -m '...' && git push origin v0.1.1
4. After successful publish, verify: npm view @intentsolutions/core versions
5. Spot-check consumer: pnpm add @intentsolutions/core@0.1.1 in a throwaway dir

Side-note: the sigstore attestation in Rekor at logIndex=1631712090 is permanent. Future audits of @intentsolutions/core@0.1.1 may show a sigstore provenance entry pointing at a tarball hash that doesn't match the eventually-published tarball (if the eventual publish re-builds from source vs reusing the tarball that was attested). Recommend: republish from THE SAME COMMIT (d9d50be) so the tarball hash matches what's already in Rekor — verify with 'shasum -a 512 intentsolutions-core-0.1.1.tgz' against the sigstore record.
close_reason: Resolved during 2026-05-26 session — root cause was empty NPM_TOKEN secret on GitHub Actions (the secret existed but value was empty after pass/gpg failed to decrypt in non-interactive Bash). Token retrieved from ~/.npmrc, set via gh secret set, then tag v0.1.1 deleted + recreated to re-fire workflow. npm view @intentsolutions/core version → 0.1.1, sigstore provenance attached at attestations URL. RESOLVED.

title: Add Parallel Change discipline to Blueprint B section 7 (expand-contract for schema additions)
description:
Per IEP thinker-panel review (Fowler finding #6, 2026-05-25). Blueprint A principle 10 says 'Schema is canon' and Blueprint B § 7 carries the normative gate-result/v1. The CHANGELOG of @intentsolutions/core is at 0.1.1 with v0.2.0 (iec-E12) in flight. Principle 10 mandates MAJOR bumps for breaking changes (no convenience minor). Good. But the question is whether EvidenceBundlePayload lands as a new optional field (expand-contract: additive, then later contract once consumers migrate) or as a required field that breaks all consumers at once.

Without an explicit Parallel Change discipline (Danilo Sato's term, which Fowler endorses), every kernel bump becomes a coordinated-deploy event across 4 consumer repos — undoing the whole point of independent versioning.

Action: Bind into Blueprint B § 7: every kernel field addition lands as optional first, ages for at least one consumer release, then becomes required only after @intentsolutions/core minor-bumps with a deprecation warning fired against the still-optional shape. This is expand-contract by spec.

Companion to bd_000-projects-uprg (P0 compat policy) — that's the EXTERNAL contract; this is the INTERNAL discipline that makes the external contract honorable.

Cross-ref: intent-eval-lab/000-docs/023-AA-AACR-thinker-panel-review-2026-05-25.md § 2.3 finding #6.
close_reason: Parallel Change / expand-contract discipline bound into Blueprint B section 7 as new normative subsection 7.0.1: kernel field additions land optional-first (Expand, MINOR bump), age at least one consumer release with a deprecation warning (Age), and become required only after a MINOR bump + the deprecation window (Contract); faster-than-aging changes mint a new major URI per section 7.2. Internal-discipline vs external-URI-contract relationship documented. Committed d3ffafa on feat/iel-blueprint-b-parallel-change. Partner-name guard clean (exit 1). title: Make state-machine spec single-sourced (Blueprint B <-> kernel transition table); add CI drift gate
description:

Kernel ships a canTransition helper; no evidence the helper's allowed-transitions table is generated from Blueprint B tables, nor that there is a test that fails the build if they drift.

Blueprint B is normative source per source-of-truth hierarchy, but if a developer edits the kernel's transition table without editing the Blueprint, the kernel ships an out-of-spec runtime and the static gate doesn't catch it. The platform's 'schema-is-canon' principle (Blueprint A § 1.2 principle 10) silently fails at the state-machine layer.

Action: either (a) make Blueprint B § 3.1 a fenced machine-readable block (e.g., state-machine.yaml referenced by the prose), generate the kernel's transition map from it, add CI drift gate; OR (b) flip the source — let kernel TS be canonical, generate the Blueprint table from a doc-extractor. title: Hash-chain Decision Records into signed append-only ledger
description:
Per IEP thinker-panel review (Kleppmann finding #1, 2026-05-25). DRs (DR-004, DR-010, DR-018, DR-022) are described as 'permanent verbatim 7-seat record' and 'unrecoverable if drift here' (DR-010 Q3 GC binding) but are plain markdown in a git repo with no content digest, no detached signature, no anchoring in the Rekor pipeline this project is building. A future contributor or rebased merge can silently mutate verbatim seat positions. The platform's governance substrate is weaker than the platform's own attestation requirements for cost-attribution/v1.

Action:
1. Compute sha256 of each NNN-AT-DECR-*.md at merge
2. Store digests in intent-eval-lab/specs/DECISION-RECORDS.md ledger (append-only, hash-chained — each entry includes prior entry's hash)
3. Sign ledger via cosign keyless
4. Anchor ledger root in rekor.sigstage.dev (dogfoods the staging pipeline)

This is exactly the merkle-log pattern Certificate Transparency uses and that you already plan to consume via Rekor.

Cross-ref: intent-eval-lab/000-docs/023-AA-AACR-thinker-panel-review-2026-05-25.md § 2.1 finding #1.

title: iaj-release-yml-branch-protection-bypass — push to protected main fails after auto-bump
description:
j-rig release.yml's auto-bump on push-to-main works correctly (build-before-test fix verified — tests pass + version computed) but fails at 'Create tag and push' step because main is branch-protected and the workflow uses bare 'git push origin HEAD' with no admin override.

Discovered 2026-05-26 immediately after PR #76 merged: workflow computed v1.1.0 (correctly — there were unreleased feat(iep-P2) commits triggering MINOR auto-bump), created the tag locally, pushed both the bump commit AND the tag in one 'git push origin HEAD v1.1.0' — TAG landed on remote (orphan, unreachable from main), commit was rejected with 'GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main'.

Orphan v1.1.0 tag cleaned up via 'git push origin :v1.1.0' (this session). Older orphan v1.0.1 tag predates this session (from earlier failed Release runs on 2026-05-20/2026-05-21/2026-05-24 — same root cause).

Fix paths:
A. Update release.yml 'Create tag and push' step to: (a) acquire temporary admin override via gh api PATCH /repos/.../branches/main/protection (per /branch-protection skill), (b) push, (c) restore protection from backup JSON. See ~/.claude/skills/branch-protection/ for canonical pattern.
B. Convert auto-bump to open-PR pattern: workflow opens a PR with the version bump commit; tag/release fires on the PR merge.

A is faster, B is cleaner. Both ship together as a sub-bead cluster.

Additional cleanup decisions for the user:
- DELETE orphan v1.0.1 tag from j-rig remote? It points at an unreachable commit from the 2026-05-21 failed run. Not in any GH release; never npm-published (release.yml has no publish step for j-rig).

Blocks proper /release v1.0.1 (or v1.1.0) for j-rig until fixed. Step 4 of the 2026-05-25 release-sweep plan now requires either path A/B above OR manual PR-based bump.

title: iar-consumer-migration: intent-rollout-gate consumes @intentsolutions/core for gate-result/v1 parsing
description:
intent-rollout-gate is the thin GH Action shell that consumes a signed EvidenceBundle + a tests/TESTING.md policy and emits a ship/no-ship decision. Currently it has local schema definitions for gate-result/v1; needs to migrate to importing the canonical GateResultV1Schema from @intentsolutions/core/validators/v1/gate-result-v1. This is the third leg of the consumer-side migration triangle (audit-harness=iah-E02, j-rig=iaj-E02, intent-rollout-gate=THIS BEAD).

## Adoption recipe

```bash
pnpm add @intentsolutions/core zod
```

### Replace local types with kernel imports
- Local gate-result/v1 predicate body type → import { GateResultV1, GateResultV1Schema } from '@intentsolutions/core/validators/v1/gate-result-v1'
- Local in-toto Statement / DSSE envelope types → import { GateResultV1Statement, DsseEnvelope } from '@intentsolutions/core'
- Local PREDICATE_URIS → import { GATE_RESULT_V1_URI, PREDICATE_URIS } from '@intentsolutions/core'

### Consumer flow (J3 from kernel JOURNEYS.md)
1. Verify DSSE envelope signatures (cosign-OIDC) — runtime concern, downstream of kernel
2. Decode base64 payload → in-toto Statement v1
3. Validate predicateType === GATE_RESULT_V1_URI (kernel-supplied constant)
4. Validate subject[].digest.sha256 === predicate.input_hash (Blueprint B § 7.4 line 814 + § 7.3 line 792 cross-reference — kernel JSDoc documents this invariant)
5. Narrow predicate to GateResultV1 via GateResultV1Schema.parse() (kernel-supplied parser; superRefine fires § 7.4 if/then advisory_severity rule automatically)
6. Apply consumer-side policy from tests/TESTING.md per § 7.6 architectural separation (NOT in kernel — consumer-owned)

### Architectural separation reminder
Per Blueprint B § 7.6: the predicate URI is immutable; policy evolves per-team. The kernel ships the predicate body parser; intent-rollout-gate ships the policy applier. Do NOT cross the streams.

title: bd auto-flush silently drops in-memory writes when .beads/ is gitignored
description:
## Summary

bd auto-flush from in-memory Dolt → .beads/issues.jsonl fails silently when the parent repo's .gitignore excludes .beads/. The failure mode: 'auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1' is emitted as a warning, but the JSONL is NOT written. Every subsequent bd command starts fresh, auto-imports the STALE JSONL into an empty Dolt DB, loses any prior in-memory writes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Workspace at ~/000-projects/.beads/ (umbrella git repo with .beads/ in .gitignore)
2. Run `bd-sync link <bead> --gh OWNER/REPO#N` — reports SUCCESS (`linked` + comment posted to GH)
3. Run `bd show <bead>` IN SAME PROCESS — link visible in NOTES (in-memory state)
4. Run `bd show <bead>` IN NEW PROCESS — link GONE
5. Repeat across 49 beads: only 11/49 persist (race depends on auto-flush ordering)

Observed in bd 1.0.4 (commit ce242a879).

## Expected Behavior

bd-sync link should persist the GitHub: line to the bead's notes field permanently, regardless of whether .beads/ is git-tracked.

## Actual Behavior

bd-sync link reports success, but the write is lost when the bd process exits because:
- bd auto-flush writes to a temp file, then runs `git add .beads/issues.jsonl`
- git add fails with exit 1 because .beads/ is gitignored
- bd treats this as a write-failure and discards the temp file
- Next bd invocation auto-imports the OLD JSONL into an empty Dolt DB, wiping any in-memory state

## Architectural Diagnosis

- bd-sync link writes to SQL in-memory state via bd update --notes
- Auto-flush step couples JSONL write WITH git add (should be decoupled — JSONL is the persistent layer; git add is a publishing concern)
- The Dolt SQL server state in .beads/dolt/ does NOT bridge across invocations the way one might expect (every `bd` command auto-imports JSONL into empty DB on startup; auto-export-from-Dolt only writes if git-add succeeds)

## Workaround Deployed

1. `bd dolt stop` to clear running server
2. Python script (/tmp/iep-mirror/patch-jsonl.py) directly appends `GitHub: jeremylongshore/<repo>#<n>` to each bead's notes in .beads/issues.jsonl
3. `bd import .beads/issues.jsonl` to upsert patched state into Dolt
4. `bd-sync status` confirms 49/49 linkage post-workaround
5. Snapshot at /tmp/iep-mirror/jsonl-final.jsonl

## Proposed Upstream Fix

(at github.com/steveyegge/beads):

1. Decouple JSONL write from git add. Write JSONL atomically (temp file + rename) and treat git add failure as a NON-FATAL warning, not a write-rollback.
2. OR: detect `.gitignore` exclusion at bd init time, warn loudly, and disable the git-add coupling automatically when the workspace is gitignored by its parent repo.

## Discovery Context

Found during IEP substrate execution 2026-05-13 (61 epics + 49 bd-sync link operations). The drift blocked bd-sync from persisting linkage on 38 of 49 beads until the workaround was deployed.
design: Upstream bug. Fix lives in bd-the-tool (Go). This bead tracks our awareness + workaround discipline until upstream lands. Reproducible in /home/jeremy/000-projects/.beads/ at any point — the .gitignore exclusion is permanent.
acceptance_criteria: EITHER (a) upstream PR lands at github.com/steveyegge/beads fixing the auto-flush vs gitignore interaction (JSONL write must succeed even when git add fails); OR (b) the workaround is documented in this repo's top-level CLAUDE.md so future contributors know to run `bd import` after any bulk bd-sync operation in gitignored workspaces. Verification: a fresh bulk `bd-sync link` of 49+ beads in this workspace results in 49/49 persistence without manual JSONL patching.

Jeremy's PR #4061 CLOSED 2026-05-21 — superseded by maphew's #4063 (MERGED 2026-05-21T23:21Z). #4063 BASED ON Jeremy's commit 313e1f82 with Based-on + Co-authored-by trailers (credit earned). PARTIAL FIX ONLY: #4063 made auto-export opt-in (default-off) but intentionally EXCLUDED the gitignored-path throttle bypass (isExportPathGitignored / shouldBypassThrottle). maphew assessment 2026-05-22T00:03Z: 'explicit opt-in workflows with export.auto=true and gitignored .beads/ can still see delayed/lost JSONL freshness inside the throttle window'. Our umbrella IS that scenario — JSONL workaround in intent-eval-platform/CLAUDE.md REMAINS LOAD-BEARING. maphew on #3848 close: 'Please reopen if this isn't the case!' — explicit invitation pending Jeremy's decision (re-engage with focused explicit-opt-in fix OR accept workaround as permanent). Full audit + candidate: ~/.contribute-system/candidates/gastownhall__beads__issue3848.md.
close_reason: Closed as MISCHARACTERIZED 2026-05-23. Empirical asciinema reproducer (~/.claude/skills/exec-decision-council/sessions/2026-05-23-beads-reengage/outputs/reproducer.cast) against gastownhall/beads@main + v1.0.4 showed the actual cause is bd's 60s default export.interval throttle, NOT a git-add silent-failure on gitignored paths. DB writes are never lost; only JSONL representation lags within throttle window; catches up on next post-throttle operation. Mitigation: 'bd config set export.interval 1s' in umbrella .beads/config.yaml (applied 2026-05-23) — verified to flush JSONL on every operation with no manual export/cp/import dance. JSONL workaround removed from intent-eval-platform/CLAUDE.md and replaced with the simple mitigation. The ISEDC council deliberation (DR 022) that led to the verify-before-claim gate that caught this is the durable lesson; the bug itself was a non-event masquerading as a known-issue. ## Concrete adoption recipe for audit-harness

### Install
```bash
pnpm add @intentsolutions/core           # types only (zero runtime cost)
pnpm add @intentsolutions/core zod       # if emitting predicate rows at runtime
```

### Replace local types with kernel imports
- Any local gate-result-shape types → import GateResultV1 from '@intentsolutions/core'
- Any local entity-shape types (EvalRun, EvidenceBundle, etc.) → import from '@intentsolutions/core'
- Any local Uuidv7/Sha256/etc. type aliases → import branded types from '@intentsolutions/core'

### Runtime validation (when emitting predicate rows)
```ts
import { GateResultV1Schema } from '@intentsolutions/core/validators/v1/gate-result-v1';
const validated = GateResultV1Schema.parse(rowPayload);  // throws on invariant violation
```

### Sanity checks to verify migration
- Run audit-harness's own tests; gate-result rows should still validate against the kernel's schema
- No more locally-defined types matching shapes in src/entities/ on the kernel side
- audit-harness's bundled tests stay green

### Architectural rules
- The kernel ships pure types in its main entry — audit-harness can freely import from main entry without pulling runtime weight
- The validators subpath (./validators/v1) requires zod ^4 as a peer
- gate-result/v1 is NORMATIVE — adding/loosening fields requires Class-1 ISEDC convening

### Migration shape (acceptance)
- audit-harness package.json: depends on @intentsolutions/core ^0.1.0
- audit-harness src/: imports from @intentsolutions/core for the relevant entities
- No regressions in audit-harness's test suite
- v0.4.0-prep PR opened against jeremylongshore/audit-harness#22

### Cross-refs
- Kernel AAR: jeremylongshore/intent-eval-core/blob/main/000-docs/001-AA-AACR-release-v0.1.0-2026-05-17.md
- Kernel CHANGELOG § Adoption notes for downstream consumers: jeremylongshore/intent-eval-core/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

description: MCP Python SDK 2.x removed Server.list_tools()/call_tool(); any server using them with an open-ended mcp>= requirement crashes on a fresh install. close_reason: Verified all four unconfirmed scan hits 2026-09-20. blog (mcp-for-beginners course content), iams (vendored framework docs) and contributing-clanker (clones of other projects) are third-party material, not ours to run: no action. searchcarriers had the real break in 5 plugin servers + pyproject (open-ended mcp, decorators called inside serve(), which no test runs, so the suite was green under both SDK lines): PR #5 merged, capped <2 in all 6 places, plus a contract test that fails on SDK 2.x and on any uncapped requirement. title: Design the auto-fix, ask-user, no-op finding-tier policy map as pure data over gate-result/v1 rows; ship nothing until a false-positive corpus exists
description: DESIGN ONLY. A policy map (data, not a pipeline stage) classifying gate findings into auto-fix / ask-user / no-op, driven off gate-result/v1 evidence. The auto-fix allowlist must be hash-pinned and restricted to provably-mechanical fixes (never .feature files, thresholds, arch rules). notes:
DESIGN (deliverable of this bead — implementation stays gated on an FP corpus):
FINDING-TIER POLICY MAP v0-draft. (1) Shape: a hash-pinned data file in the consumer repo, tiers.v1.yaml, mapping gate-result/v1 coordinates (gate_id + rule/pattern id) -> tier in {auto-fix, ask-user, no-op}. Pure classification over evidence rows; NEVER a pipeline stage, never consulted by the gates themselves. (2) Defaults: every unmapped finding = ask-user; no-op only for rows already result:ADVISORY severity info. (3) auto-fix eligibility (ALL required): fix is provably mechanical (deterministic rewrite, no judgment); target file is NOT in the harness-hash denominator (never .feature, thresholds, arch rules, TESTING.md policy, CI workflows); the fixer is idempotent and emits its own gate-result row; the (finding,fixer) pair has a measured FP rate <=5% over a labeled corpus per docs/gate-promotion.md; an engineer pin in tests/TESTING.md names the pair. (4) The map file itself enters .harness-hash-extra-patterns so tier changes REFUSE without re-pin. (5) Consumption point: a post-run classifier over worktree-run/audit/scan row output — reporting only until the corpus exists. Rationale trail: Torvalds seat objected to the tier wholesale; Beck+Hickey wanted it narrow/earned; this design answers the objection with the stack's own earned-enforcement discipline. Nothing ships until fp-rate proves the first (finding,fixer) pair.

title: Decide the fate of the plugin's uncommitted governed-brain.cjs rebundle churn sitting on main
description:
FOUND during the 2026-07-29 repo sweep: bobs-big-brain-plugin has an UNCOMMITTED
modification to plugin-runtime/governed-brain.cjs sitting directly on `main`
(not a feature branch). 476 changed lines.

CHARACTERIZED (so nobody assumes it is the Track C rebundle):
  - 432 of the 476 changed lines are esbuild SOURCE-PATH comments/strings
    changing shape only, e.g.
      -// ../../../../../000-projects/bobs-big-brain-registrar/packages/store/dist/schema.js
      +// ../bobs-big-brain-registrar/packages/store/dist/schema.js
  - ZERO references to dense / sqlite-vec / EmbeddingGemma in the diff.

So this is almost certainly incidental churn from running the bundler at a
different working-directory depth than the last committed build — NOT the
gybo.4 / Track C rebundle (which is supposed to pick up dense B4 from the
registrar). It should not be mistaken for that work being done.

DECISION NEEDED (owner: plugin agent / Jeremy):
  (a) DISCARD (`git checkout -- plugin-runtime/governed-brain.cjs`) as meaningless
      path churn, then do the real Track C rebundle deliberately on a branch; or
  (b) COMMIT it if the shorter relative paths are actually preferred as the
      canonical build output (they are cleaner and less machine-specific — a
      reasonable position), in which case pin HOW the bundle is built (from which
      cwd) so the paths stop flip-flopping between builds; or
  (c) Investigate the ~44 non-path lines first — I did not examine them
      individually, so I am not claiming the diff is 100% cosmetic.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: governed-brain.cjs is the SHIPPED plugin runtime.
Uncommitted edits to it on `main` mean the local runtime and the published artifact
disagree, and a bundle whose diff is dominated by absolute-path leakage
(`/home/jeremy/000-projects/...`) is machine-specific output — worth deciding on
deliberately rather than letting the next build flip it back.

Do NOT bundle this decision into an unrelated PR. Track C proper is
bd_000-projects-gybo.4, still blocked on gybo.1 (registrar reconcile).

Sweep did not modify the plugin tree (single-writer discipline).

title: Keep qmd updated in the Bob's Big Brain system: add a version-drift check + update cadence
description: Standing requirement (Jeremy 2026-07-26): the runtime qmd used by the governed brain must not silently lag upstream. Root cause found this session: the global/runtime qmd on PATH (~/.bun/bin/qmd) was pinned ^2.0.1 and had drifted to 2.0.1 while npm latest + the bobs-big-brain-registrar pin were 2.5.3 — so a brain_govern reindex silently skipped in one environment and new memories were briefly unsearchable. FIXED now: bun add -g @tobilu/qmd@latest -> 2.5.3, brain_search validated (score 1.0). REMAINING (the 'stay updated' mechanism): (1) a drift check comparing installed qmd (qmd --version) vs npm latest (npm view @tobilu/qmd version) AND the registrar pin, exit non-zero on mismatch; (2) wire it into the estate's existing scheduled-automation + Slack alerting so drift pings instead of being found mid-session; (3) decide the update cadence + whether to 'bun pm trust' the node-llama-cpp/tree-sitter postinstalls when the dense-semantic (B4) path is wired. acceptance_criteria: Pilot run producing ≥1 cluster + ≥10 reviewed annotations (human-accepted or human-rejected) via the D6-D10 + D12 path. Acceptance: cluster quality metrics meet J2's threshold + annotation audit log is verifiable.

title: Run trace-ingestion pilot on the selected agent + repo
design: Cross-reference D1-D5.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot run producing ≥1 day of fixture traces ingested via the D1-D5 path. Acceptance: trace count ≥ J2's threshold + no failed ingests in the run + Mission Control projection (F2) reflects the new coverage.

title: Recovery and rollback test plan
design: Owner-gated RTO/RPO values.
acceptance_criteria: Plan at `000-docs/trace-intel-I15-recovery-tests.md`. For every D-series component: (1) restore-from-backup test, (2) rollback-to-prior-version test, (3) data-loss prevention test (in-progress ingest doesn't lose traces on process crash), (4) RTO + RPO targets documented + tested. Acceptance: every component passes the four tests; RTO ≤1h, RPO ≤15min for trace data.

title: Acceptance and dogfood test plan
design: Cross-reference the J1-J10 pilot plan.
acceptance_criteria: Plan at `000-docs/trace-intel-I14-acceptance-tests.md`. The system must be dogfooded on a real (non-fixture) agent + repo for 7 consecutive days before production adoption (J14). Acceptance: the dogfood run produces ≥100 traces ingested + ≥10 annotations accepted + ≥1 signed evidence receipt + Mission Control projection renders without error.

title: Integration-test plan across IEP, JRig, rollout-gate, Evidence Bench, AGP, BBB, and Mission Control
design: This is the system's smoke test. It must be runnable from CI.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I13-integration-tests.md`. End-to-end: trace ingest → cluster → sample → annotate → AI propose → human accept → taxonomy mutation → dataset → regression → JRig exec → rollout-gate decision → Evidence Bench verify → Mission Control projection. Acceptance: a single `pnpm test:e2e` (or equivalent) runs the full chain end-to-end with one fixture set.

title: Security and privacy test plan
design: Cross-reference the IEP disclosure-gate.sh.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I12-security-tests.md`. For D22: redaction-at-ingest test (fake secret in trace → redacted in canonical store), AGP-fail test (AGP down → 403 + audit entry), deletion test (owner approval + audit + tombstone metadata). Acceptance: passes against the IEP disclosure-gate hard-fail pattern set.

title: Evidence-signature validation test plan
design: Cross-reference C13 (evidence contract) + the Evidence Bench's verification rules.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I11-evidence-signature-tests.md`. For D21: chain-validation test (10 chained receipts + verify), tamper-detection test (modify one receipt + assert verification fails), policy-version test (receipt carries the signing-time policy). Acceptance: passes.

title: Regression-generation test plan
design: Cross-reference the JRig existing tests.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I10-regression-generation-tests.md`. For D19/D20: human-accepted-source test (rejects AI-proposed-only annotations), EvalRun-emission test (10 cases → 10 runs + 10 signed receipts). Acceptance: passes.

title: Dataset reproducibility test plan
design: Cross-reference C9 (dataset contract).
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I9-dataset-reproducibility-tests.md`. For D17/D18: rebuild-from-source test (rebuild dataset bytes from declared inputs, assert content_hash equality), version-history test (3 versions + each rebuildable). Acceptance: passes.

title: Sampling-bias and coverage test plan
design: Cross-reference C8 (sampling contract).
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I8-sampling-bias-tests.md`. For D15/D16: determinism test (same input + same params → same decision), coverage test (every taxonomy node gets ≥1 sample), bias test (uniform sampler produces statistically uniform output). Acceptance: passes.

title: Taxonomy-version and migration test plan
design: Cross-reference the IEP event-taxonomy work in `bd_000-projects-fqtm`.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I7-taxonomy-migration-tests.md`. For D13/D14: MAJOR bump + migration application test (10 affected annotations), reversibility test (rebuild from signed receipt), suppression test (deprecated nodes still queryable with a warning). Acceptance: passes.

title: Human-approval enforcement test plan
design: Cross-reference the AGP authority model.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I6-human-approval-tests.md`. For H2/H4/H5: role-restriction tests, co-sign enforcement test (N=2 default for taxonomy), audit-log-presence test (every accept/reject produces an audit entry). Acceptance: passes.

title: Annotation-integrity test plan
design: Cross-reference the IEP summarize.py reviewer-override pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I5-annotation-integrity-tests.md`. For D8-D12: CQRS separation test (audit log immutable, current state is projection), AI-proposal-isolation test (proposals never mutate canonical), human-override test (human accept produces a signed receipt). Acceptance: passes.

title: Clustering-quality test plan
design: Use sklearn's clustering benchmarks as the basis for synthetic fixtures with known ground-truth labels.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I4-clustering-quality-tests.md`. For D6/D7: stability re-run test (same input + same params → same cluster_id), quality-metric threshold test (silhouette ≥ 0.2 + ari ≥ 0.5 with human gold). Acceptance: passes against the 100-trace fixture set.

title: Trace-ingestion failure-test plan
design: Cross-reference the IEP fail-closed posture.
acceptance_criteria: Plan + tests at `000-docs/trace-intel-I3-ingestion-failure-tests.md`. For each D1-D5 component: at least 5 failure-mode tests (network down, malformed JSON, schema violation, lineage corruption, permission denial). Acceptance: every D-series implementation passes all 5 tests.

title: Schema and contract-test plan for every C-series contract
design: JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Use the IEP `validate-skills-schema.py` pattern as a template.
acceptance_criteria: Plan at `000-docs/trace-intel-I2-schema-test-plan.md`. For each C1-C19 contract: a JSON Schema fixture (positive + negative examples), an expected-validation-result, and a CI step that runs the fixtures against the latest published schema. Acceptance: all C-series schemas ship with at least 5 negative examples each.

title: Unit-test plan + harness for the trace-intel capability
design: Use the existing IEP test harness pattern.
acceptance_criteria: Plan at `000-docs/trace-intel-I1-unit-test-plan.md` + test harness PR. Must declare: (1) coverage targets (≥80% line, ≥70% branch), (2) test-file naming convention, (3) fixtures + factories location, (4) mocking strategy for external services, (5) CI integration. Acceptance: a sample D-series implementation lands ≥80% coverage on first CI run.
notes:
Group I — Testing and validation.
Each I-bead is paired with its target D/E/F/G/H-bead. I13 e2e test must be runnable from CI. I14 dogfood = 7 consecutive days of real usage. I15 RTO ≤1h + RPO ≤15min for trace data.

title: Add cited retrieval for historical evaluation lessons
design: Cross-reference the existing BBB search (`brain_search` MCP) + the lineage API (D4).
acceptance_criteria: Retrieval endpoint: GET /bbb/cite?query=X returns the matching BBBKnowledgeEntry records with their full citation chain (trace + annotation + evidence receipt) and the lineage proof. Integration test that queries for a known historical pattern and verifies the returned entries cite non-empty source traces.

title: Add expiry, supersession, and correction rules for BBB entries from this program
design: Default expiry: 1 year. Owner-overridable.
acceptance_criteria: Lifecycle service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) every BBBKnowledgeEntry (C15) carries an expiry_at, (2) on expiry, the entry is moved to a tombstone table (not deleted — preserves audit), (3) supersession creates a new entry that points at the superseded one (C15.supersedes_entry_id), (4) correction creates a new entry with the corrected content + a citation_trace_id of the entry it corrects. Integration test covering each lifecycle event.

title: Link BBB knowledge to source traces and evidence
design: Cross-reference the lineage service. Citations are append-only.
acceptance_criteria: Linker service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) every BBBKnowledgeEntry (C15) carries citation_trace_ids + citation_evidence_receipt_ids arrays, (2) the citation chain is verifiable via the lineage API (D4), (3) integration test that walks the chain from a BBB entry back to its source trace.

title: Correlate commits, PRs, agent runs, evaluations, and releases
design: Use the GitHub commit SHA as the join key (cross-reference D4 lineage). For agent runs that don't have a direct commit SHA, join via PR base_ref.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation endpoint: GET /correlations?commit_sha=X returns {pr_id, agent_run_ids, eval_run_ids, evidence_receipt_ids, release_tag}. Mission Control renders this in the existing commit-detail view. Integration test with fixture trace data + GH data.

title: Detect orphan traces, annotations, evaluations, and evidence
design: Cross-reference the D4 lineage service (every canonical object MUST have a lineage chain). Detection = reverse-walk the lineage graph.
acceptance_criteria: Detection endpoint: GET /detections/orphans returns objects that exist but have no lineage link to any owning repo or agent. Mission Control consumes this. Integration test ingesting orphan objects and asserting they appear in the output.

title: Detect stale evaluations and datasets
design: Cross-reference F5 (dataset coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Detection endpoint: GET /detections/stale-evaluations returns repos whose latest_dataset_age_days exceeds a configurable threshold (default 90d). Mission Control consumes this.

title: Detect repositories with missing trace coverage
design: Cross-reference F2 (coverage projection). Detection = projection + registry join.
acceptance_criteria: Detection endpoint exposed: GET /detections/missing-trace-coverage returns the list of repos whose trace_count_last_7d = 0 AND that are listed as owning-agent-id repositories per the IEP registry. Mission Control consumes this and surfaces it in a 'trace-intel gaps' view.

title: Project evidence-receipt validity
design: Cross-reference C14 + C13.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint: GET /projections/evidence-validity?repo=X returns {valid_receipts_last_30d, invalid_receipts_last_30d, validity_status}. Integration test.

title: Project evaluation and rollout status
design: Cross-reference C14 + C12.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint: GET /projections/rollout-status?repo=X returns {pass_count_last_30d, fail_count_last_30d, override_count_last_30d, policy_version}. Integration test.

title: Project dataset and regression coverage
design: Cross-reference C14.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint: GET /projections/dataset-coverage?repo=X returns {latest_dataset_age_days, regression_case_count_last_30d, eval_run_count_last_30d}. Integration test with fixture datasets.

title: Project taxonomy versions and drift
design: Cross-reference C14.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint exposed in the C17-chosen repo: GET /projections/taxonomy-drift?repo=X returns {current_taxonomy_version, latest_taxonomy_version, drift_status}. Mission Control renders this. Integration test with repos at different taxonomy versions.

title: Project annotation and review status
design: Cross-reference C14.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint exposed in the C17-chosen repo: GET /projections/annotation-status?repo=X returns {accepted_last_7d, rejected_last_7d, ai_proposed_pending, reviewer_count}. Mission Control consumes this. Integration test with fixture accepted/rejected annotations.

title: Project trace coverage by repository and agent
design: Cross-reference C14 (projection contract). Polled, not pushed.
acceptance_criteria: Projection endpoint exposed in the C17-chosen repo: GET /projections/trace-coverage?repo=X returns {trace_count_last_7d, agent_ids[], gap_status}. Mission Control consumes this and renders it in the existing readiness+risk view. Integration test that ingests fixture traces + asserts the projection updates within 1 hour.

title: Register the capability and all owning repositories in Mission Control
design: Mission Control's existing capability registration pattern. Cross-reference the intent-os Mission Control skill (`~/.claude/skills/mission-control`).
acceptance_criteria: Capability registered in intent-os Mission Control with: capability name (TraceIntelligence), capability version, owning repos (per C17), data sources it depends on, and the projection contracts it consumes (per C14). Owner sign-off required.
notes:
Group F — Mission Control and estate governance.
Mission Control consumes IEP-owned projection APIs (C14); it does NOT compute projections itself. F12 readiness+risk views require F2-F11 as upstream.

title: Publish versioned platform documentation and schemas
design: Versioned docs. Use the existing IEP docs framework.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation PR merged into the IEP docs site. Must include: (1) every C-series contract spec rendered as HTML, (2) every D-series implementation's public API, (3) every E-series integration guide, (4) a CHANGELOG that maps every version bump to the underlying ADR. Site must build via `pnpm docs:build` and deploy via the existing IEP docs CI workflow. Acceptance: `pnpm docs:build` exits 0.

title: Integrate platform APIs with the IEP evaluation dashboard
design: Cross-reference the existing IEP dashboard for layout patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard PR into `intent-eval-platform/intent-eval-dashboard`. The dashboard must surface: trace coverage per repo (from C14/F2), annotation throughput (from F3), taxonomy version + drift (from F4), dataset freshness (from F5), evidence validity (from F7). Integration test that hits each endpoint and asserts the dashboard renders without error.

title: Integrate generated regression cases with JRig execution
design: JRig's existing run command gets a `--from-regression-case` flag. Cross-reference D20 (implement evaluator-generation workflow).
acceptance_criteria: Integration PR into `intent-eval-platform/j-rig-binary-eval`. JRig must execute a RegressionCase (C10) end-to-end and emit an EvalRun (C11) per execution. Integration test that feeds 10 fixture RegressionCases and asserts 10 EvalRuns + 10 signed evidence receipts.

title: Integrate accepted annotations with JRig criteria
design: Cross-reference `bd_000-projects-214c` (JRig coordination) and `bd_000-projects-0r8m` (SkillVersion + signed evidence reports). JRig's existing expected_outcome shape must be extended, not replaced.
acceptance_criteria: Integration PR into `intent-eval-platform/j-rig-binary-eval`. JRig must accept an annotation as input to a binary-skill evaluation (C4 AnnotationRecord + source trace_id). Integration test that runs JRig with an annotation-derived expected_outcome and asserts the result is reproducible.

title: Integrate normalized traces with existing IEP evaluation schemas
design: Cross-reference `bd_000-projects-ig4h` (eval research-driven scoring layer). The new schema is additive — existing evaluators that only consume text must still work.
acceptance_criteria: Integration PR merged into the IEP estate. The IEP evaluator must consume a normalized trace (C1) as input, not just the existing text-only skill content. Integration test that feeds a fixture normalized trace through an existing evaluator and asserts the score is unchanged for backward-compatible cases AND new tool-call sequences score correctly. Migration guide for any existing dataset that needs to be re-normalized.

title: Implement uncertainty and coverage sampling strategies
design: Plugin interface (TypeScript or Python) so a future strategy can be added without modifying the engine. Owner-gated strategy choices.
acceptance_criteria: Strategy implementations in the C17-chosen repo. Must implement at least: (1) uncertainty — entropy-based, requires D11 proposals, (2) coverage-gap — ensures every taxonomy node gets a target sample count, (3) committee-disagreement — uses ≥2 different model_ids and samples where they disagree. Each strategy MUST be a plugin matching the C8 SamplingPolicy schema. Unit tests for each. The contract is the wire format; the implementations are open for replacement.

title: Implement adaptive sampling engine
design: Default uncertainty sampler: per-cluster entropy over AI proposals (if proposals exist) OR coverage-gap (if not). Strategy choice deferred to B12.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) accept a SamplingPolicy (C8), (2) on a batch of trace_ids, return a SamplingDecision (C8) matching the policy's strategy (uniform / uncertainty / diversity / coverage-gap / committee-disagreement), (3) be deterministic (same input + same params_hash → same decision), (4) integration test that runs the same policy twice on the same trace set and asserts identical sampled_trace_ids arrays.

title: Implement annotation user interface
design: Self-host the UI per C17 + C18 decisions. Default: a thin React app served by the same container as the annotation backend, exposed via the VPS Caddy ingress.
acceptance_criteria: Annotation UI at the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) display traces from a SamplingDecision (C8) in a reviewer queue, (2) show AI-proposed labels alongside the trace (C6 contract), (3) require the reviewer to issue an explicit accept|reject|revise decision (C4) before moving to the next trace, (4) show the full audit history of any annotation the reviewer is acting on, (5) role-aware (only taxonomy-editors can mutate taxonomy nodes; only dataset-editors can mark a record as ready for dataset inclusion; default reviewers accept/reject only). Playwright/Cypress integration tests for happy-path + each role's restrictions.

title: Implement deterministic cluster-quality checks
design: Threshold defaults are documented and owner-overridable via AGP policy. Threshold values themselves are NOT architecture — pick the defaults in this bead, get owner sign-off, document in the runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Quality-check service in the C17-chosen repo. Must compute at least silhouette_score and ari_vs_human_gold where human gold is available, store the result on the Cluster object (C3), and emit a rejection event if any quality metric falls below a configurable threshold (default silhouette ≥ 0.2; default ari_vs_human_gold ≥ 0.5 — owner-overridable). Integration test with a fixture cluster where quality fails, asserting the rejection event is emitted.

title: Implement initial clustering pipeline
design: Algorithm choice deferred to B12. Default implementation: HDBSCAN over sentence-transformer embeddings (matches the BGE-small embedding server in `~/bin/lib/minimax-agent.py` sibling — see kilo embeddings for context). Owner-gated algorithm choice.
acceptance_criteria: Clustering service in the C17-chosen repo. Must: (1) ingest a batch of trace_ids + their normalized representations, (2) emit a Cluster object matching C3 schema (with algorithm_version + params_hash + quality_metrics), (3) store the cluster with stability re-run field (C3), (4) expose POST /clusters (input trace_ids + policy params) → Cluster object. Determinism test: same input + same params → same cluster_id. Integration test using a fixture set of 100 synthetic traces.

title: Implement trace query and retrieval APIs
design: REST + JSON. OpenAPI spec published. Cursor-based pagination to handle large trace sets.
acceptance_criteria: Read API in the C17-chosen repo. Must expose: GET /traces (time-range + agent_id + taxonomy filter), GET /traces/{trace_id}, GET /traces/{id}/annotations, GET /traces/{id}/datasets, GET /traces/{id}/evidence. Each endpoint MUST require AGP-mediated authorization (H1). Pagination + rate limit + audit-log entries per C19. Integration tests covering happy-path + auth-fail + audit-log entry.

title: Produce competitor and open-source comparison matrix across all B-series research areas
design: Build the matrix from the B1-B10 reports + the existing IEP research (`bd_000-projects-ig4h`, `bd_000-projects-l44w`, `bd_000-projects-fqtm`). Cite every cell.
acceptance_criteria: Comparison matrix at `000-docs/trace-intel-B11-competitor-matrix.md` and machine-readable `000-docs/trace-intel-B11-competitor-matrix.json`. For each B1-B10 research area: at least 3 named alternatives compared on license, cost model, vendor lock-in risk, deterministic guarantees, maintenance velocity (commits/month over last 12mo), and active community size. Must explicitly call out which options are 'commercial SaaS', 'self-host open-source', or 'in-house'. NO recommendations — that's B12.

title: Research privacy, secrets, and sensitive-trace handling
design: Owner-gated. No policy decision is made by this bead — only the research base for the owner. Threat model must include 'annotation leakage' and 'evidence-receipt leakage' as distinct concerns.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B10-privacy-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct privacy patterns (prompt-redaction at the ingest boundary, encryption-at-rest with KMS, per-recipient decryption, anonymized trace-store with re-identification-only-on-policy-match) with at least 1 named implementation per pattern. Must surface the legal/regulatory considerations (GDPR Art. 17 right-to-erasure, US state privacy laws, HIPAA for healthcare-adjacent agents) and recommend a default posture. Must specifically address the threat model of 'AI-assisted labels inadvertently retaining snippets of trace text.'

title: Research signed evidence and reproducibility mechanisms
design: Cross-reference `bd_000-projects-0r8m` (SkillVersion + signed evidence reports) and `bd_000-projects-h08j.7` (Evidence Bundle signature verification, currently DEFERRED). Note that any choice must produce a verifiable artifact consumable by Evidence Bench.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B9-evidence-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct evidence-signing approaches (Sigstore cosign, in-toto attestations, PGP-signed JSON, Ed25519 JSON-LD signature with hash-chained audit log, S3 + KMS attestations) with at least 1 named implementation per approach. For each: signature algorithm + key custodian model, hash-chaining guarantees, signature verification cost, open-source tooling, and integration with the existing Evidence Bench design.

title: Research executable eval and regression frameworks
design: Cross-reference `bd_000-projects-214c` (j-rig-binary-eval coordination) and `bd_000-projects-ig4h` (eval research-driven scoring layer). JRig is the existing primary framework; this research evaluates whether to keep it as the canonical binary-skill eval framework or supplement it.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B8-eval-framework-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct executable eval frameworks (JRig-style binary-skill eval, jepa-style agent simulation, deterministic-script eval, LLM-judge + rubric, pytest-style assertion eval) with at least 1 named tool per framework. For each: deterministic-execution guarantees, human-reviewer gating, integration with the IEP scoring layer (`bd_000-projects-ig4h`), integration with JRig binary-skill harness, and how the framework records which model version produced the score.

title: Research dataset versioning, lineage, and reproducibility patterns
design: The Intent Eval Platform already uses Dolt (per existing IEP architecture). Include Dolt-native dataset versioning as a serious option. Also note the Skill Refiner SkillVersion entity + signed evidence reports pattern from `bd_000-projects-0r8m` — its dataset-equivalent contract is the technical starting point.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B7-dataset-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct dataset-versioning approaches (DVC, Pachyderm, lakeFS, git-LFS, Dolthub-style Dolt commits, HuggingFace Datasets revisions) with at least 1 named tool per approach. For each: lineage capture (does it know which annotations built this dataset?), reproducibility (can I rebuild the dataset bytes from the declared inputs?), cost model (storage + bandwidth per version), open-source vs SaaS, and how it handles binary vs text vs structured data.

title: Research failure-taxonomy governance and versioning patterns
design: Treat the IEP event-taxonomy work in `bd_000-projects-fqtm` (iel-E15b) as an adjacent existing capability and assess integration. Do not duplicate or close iel-E15b; reference it.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B6-taxonomy-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct taxonomy-governance patterns (single-owner with versions + migration, federated with co-evolution, GitOps-stored taxonomy, attribute-set with Miros/TagUI-style faceted browsing) with at least 1 example per pattern. For each: how taxonomy mutation is gated (who approves?), how supersession works, how drift is detected, how reproducibility of historical annotations is preserved. Must recommend a taxonomy-storage location (in repo, in a registry, in evidence receipts).

title: Research AI-assisted annotation proposal systems
design: Apply the IEP rule: AI proposes, humans approve. The research must document how each approach enforces this rule (e.g., proposal-only data plane that never mutates canonical state). Treat MiniMax-M3 as one viable proposal LLM but not the only option. Cross-reference with the IEP `summarize.py` + the IEP refiner provider at `intent-eval-platform/j-rig-binary-eval/packages/refiner/src/providers.ts`.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B5-ai-annotation-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct AI-proposal approaches (zero-shot label via chat completion, few-shot in-context examples, retrieval-augmented from accepted-history, fine-tuned classifier) with at least 1 named system per approach. For each: confidence-calibration method, audit-trail requirements, vendor lock-in risk, cost per batch, and concrete prompts or model specifications. Must include a 'human-override rate' target so the team can later measure when AI proposals are correct vs rejected.

title: Research adaptive and uncertainty-based sampling strategies
design: Cite Settles' active-learning literature (Settles 2009, 2012). Treat the IEP+j-rig binary-skill evaluation flow (`bd_000-projects-0r8m`) as an existing concrete case where these strategies will be applied. Do not implement.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B4-sampling-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct sampling strategies (uniform random, uncertainty-based, diversity/Margin-based, coverage-gap-based, active-learning-committee disagreement) with concrete pseudocode or paper citations for each. For each: determinism guarantees, bias-risk, cold-start behavior, cost per batch, and integration with cluster output from B2. Must recommend a sampling-strategy decision matrix (which strategy fits which situation).

title: Research annotation platforms and labeling workflows for agent traces
design: Compare both self-hostable (Label Studio, Argilla) and SaaS (Scale, Labelbox) options. Self-host defaults to higher priority per Intent Solutions' vendor-neutral doctrine. BBB's existing `brain_review` workflow (in `~/bin/teamkb-compile-daily.sh` per `bd_000-projects-slfo`) is the in-house model — assess it as an option too.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B3-annotation-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 5 distinct annotation-platform approaches (Label Studio, Argilla, Prodigy, Scale, custom MVC on top of a Postgres+JSONB store, BBB-style agent-mediated review) with at least 1 named tool per approach. For each: human-reviewer identity model (how is reviewer identity captured?), approval workflow expressiveness (can we require a second reviewer for taxonomy mutations?), audit-log durability, license, self-host complexity, and integration cost with IEP + BBB.

title: Research trace clustering and similarity analysis algorithms
design: Vendor-neutral. Cite OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoints, sentence-transformers, HDBSCAN, leidenalg, faiss, qdrant-client, ladybugdb graph algorithms. Note: this bead produces a comparison matrix; tool selection happens later in C3 + C18.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B2-clustering-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 4 distinct clustering approaches (k-means, HDBSCAN, embedding-then-UMAP, semantic-dedup, graph-community-detection) with at least 2 named toolkits per approach. For each: license, deterministic guarantees (does running twice on the same input produce identical clusters?), evaluation metrics (silhouette, ARI, NMI), cost per cluster re-run, and embedding dependency. Must include a 'reproducibility + non-determinism' section addressing how each approach handles stochasticity.

title: Research trace collection and observability patterns for agent traces
design: Vendor-neutral research only. Do not pick a tool. Use web search + GitHub search + the existing `bd_000-projects-awuw.2` (Claude Code native OTel) and `bd_000-projects-ktm0` (dogfood OTel as IEP data source) findings as starting evidence. Cite every claim.
acceptance_criteria: Research report at `000-docs/trace-intel-B1-trace-collection-research.md`. Must enumerate at least 5 distinct trace-source categories (Claude Code native OTel, vendor SDKs, OTLP-compatible backends, in-process wrappers, log-file scraping) with at least 2 named tools per category. For each tool list: license, self-host vs SaaS, OTel compatibility, agent-trace fidelity (does it capture tool calls + reasoning or only text), trace volume scaling characteristics, and evidence-pointer URL or commit. Must include a 'deferred decisions' section listing which choices are NOT made by this bead and require owner input later.
notes:
Group B — External research and build-vs-adopt.
Vendor-neutral research only. No tool selection made by research; every research output must enumerate ≥3 alternatives + cite evidence. B12's owner-signed recommendation is the formal entry gate to Group C.

title: Reconcile the A3 inventory against Mission Control's estate registry and estate graph
design: Mission Control estate data lives in intent-os (Caddy + Dolt + LadybugDB per intent-os runbook). Read the estate registry via the documented MC API (or via direct Dolt SQL if the API is insufficient). Compare against A3 inventory on name + repo + path. Output a delta table. The reconciliation surfaces the gap between what Mission Control thinks the estate looks like and what the audit proved it actually looks like.
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation report at `000-docs/trace-intel-A7-mc-reconciliation.md`.
