title: Fleet LLM provider-fragility: 2 of 3 nightly providers exhausted within 24h
description:
## Why

2026-07-23 22:36Z → 2026-07-24 03:30Z: three nightly LLM-backed jobs failed in sequence, all on HTTP 402 'Payment Required':
- DeepSeek (prescreen LLM, PR #1126): fixed by swapping summarize.py to MiniMax.
- Grok Build (teamkb-compile-daily): today's run failed 03:30:03 with 'grok -p exited non-zero (1) after 9s'.
- Grok Build (blog-backfill-daily): same outage pattern (today's beat updated but .ok not).

The dead-man's-switch automation-liveness-sweep correctly detected both Grok failures and pinged healthchecks.io /fail. The alert is the system telling us the truth, not a bug in the sweep.

## What's fragile

teamkb-compile-daily and blog-backfill-daily depend on  as a SHELL BINARY that runs a multi-turn agent (skills, MCP, file I/O). MiniMax-M3 is a chat endpoint — no headless agent shell. So 'swap to MiniMax' is NOT a 1-line fix for these jobs; it requires building a new agent harness.

## Three real options

1. Top up Grok Build + DeepSeek. ~5 min at the dashboards. Recovers tonight.
2. Build a MiniMax-backed headless agent shell. Multi-day work. Real fix at the architecture level.
3. Accept the fragility + lower the liveness sweep's failure sensitivity. Bad — hides the problem.

## Recommendation

Option 1 now (immediate recovery). Option 2 as a separate bead (real fix at the architecture level). Owner action required: top up Grok Build usage at the Grok dashboard.

- Memory: feedback-no-redundant-rotation-asks.md (NEVER propose rotating the Tailscale + GH PAT tokens reserved in secrets.prod.sops.yaml)
- CLAUDE.md § Dev box stability / VPS-as-the-home
- Runbook: ~/000-projects/intent-os/ops/alert-routing.md
- Alert-floor epic 1.5: spine-u1a.4 owner gate

title: Publish a refiner release that carries score --provider forwarding + op-tolerance, and add groq/nvidia/openai to the j-rig eval provider presets, so the packaged CLI runs the full Skill Refiner loop on free models
description:
The full Skill Refiner loop (bootstrap→propose→apply→score→accept→render-report) was demonstrated end-to-end on free/cheap models (propose on Groq llama-3.3-70b, score on DeepSeek deepseek-v4-flash, authoritative accept() REJECT: no-behavioral-improvement, self-contained HTML evidence report rendered). Two integration gaps block this from being a one-command user experience via the packaged @intentsolutions/jrig-cli:

1. The packaged CLI pins @intentsolutions/refiner@^0.2.0 (published), which lacks BOTH the score --provider forwarding (already in workspace source) AND the op-tolerance/JSON-mode fixes on PR #203. The workspace refiner works (proven via a direct runner); the published one silently fails scoring on non-Anthropic providers (forwards --models sonnet, no --provider → eval runs a bad model id → empty output → behavioral 0.0). Fix: after PR #203 merges, publish a new @intentsolutions/refiner, bump the CLI dep, republish jrig-cli.

2. The j-rig eval command's provider presets are only deepseek|kimi|moonshot|openrouter|anthropic — it never gained groq/nvidia/openai, which the refiner provider registry DOES have. So 'refine score --provider groq' resolves in the refiner but then shells 'j-rig eval --provider groq' which eval rejects. The refiner registry claims to byte-mirror eval's names but now diverges. Fix: add groq/nvidia/openai presets to eval OR document the divergence + restrict refine score --provider to the eval-supported intersection.

Also: refine score needs an eval-spec.yaml in the skill dir (the bootstrapped eval-set is prompts-only and isn't wired into j-rig eval as a --spec). Consider having bootstrap emit a runnable eval-spec.yaml, or have score pass the bootstrapped set to eval.

Packaged-CLI drift root cause = CLI's plain ^0.2.0 range resolving the PUBLISHED refiner not the workspace one; fixed via workspace:^ (rewrites to ^0.3.0 at publish). VERIFIED: clean 'npm install @intentsolutions/jrig-cli@0.2.0' resolves refiner@0.3.0, eval --help lists openai, refine score --help carries --provider. PR #204 (Gemini clean, CI 13/13, 1407 tests). Deferred: eval-spec.yaml bootstrapping (bootstrapped set is prompts-only).

title: Make the refiner's naive-in-context JSON extraction robust to non-Anthropic model output (DeepSeek returns fenced/prefixed JSON)
description: Surfaced 2026-07-10 running the Skill Refiner demo on a real skill via --provider deepseek (the new provider seam, PR j-rig #203). 'refine propose --strategy naive-in-context --provider deepseek' fails with 'Error: no JSON object found in completion' — DeepSeek (deepseek-v4-flash) wraps its JSON in markdown fences or adds prose, and the naive-in-context strategy's JSON extraction expects a bare JSON object (Anthropic-style). Fix: make the extraction robust — strip ```json fences, find the first/last balanced {...}, tolerate leading prose. Also seen: skill-opt-style --provider deepseek returns 0 ops (valid conservative outcome, no bug). Repo: j-rig-binary-eval, packages/refiner strategies.

title: Spike: build a deepsec -> gate-result/v1 Evidence Bundle adapter so agent-powered security findings feed the IEP rollout gate
description:
deepsec (github.com/vercel-labs/deepsec, Apache-2.0, 4.8k stars) is an agent-powered code-vulnerability scanner: regex matchers (cheap prefilter) -> AI coding agent investigates -> cheaper-model triage/revalidate -> findings exported as md/json/metrics, with a --diff PR-gating mode. Architecturally it is the SAME pipeline as j-rig (deterministic prefilter -> agent eval -> triage -> gate), pointed at source-code security instead of agent-artifact behavior. Crucially it EXPORTS findings but does NOT sign/attest them.

Per DR-010 Q3 unification thesis (every validator emits a gate-result/v1 Evidence Bundle), deepsec is a natural Tier-1 convergence INPUT: a SECURITY-dimension producer that the IEP rollout gate could consume alongside audit-harness's deterministic gates, and whose evidence IEP's attestation layer (cosign -> Rekor, the thing deepsec lacks) could SIGN.

SPIKE DELIVERABLES:
1. Field-mapping doc: deepsec finding JSON -> gate-result/v1 (severity -> verdict/decision; finding -> criterion; git committer + commit_sha -> correlation/provenance; deepsec run -> EvalRun).
2. Thin adapter (emit-evidence-from-deepsec) that turns deepsec export into gate-result/v1 rows, schema-bound to @intentsolutions/core schemas/v1/gate-result.schema.json.
3. Demo: deepsec --diff on a sample repo -> bundle rows -> intent-rollout-gate ship/no-ship decision -> cosign/Rekor signed security evidence.
4. Evaluate borrowable cost-tiering (cheap regex prefilter + cheaper-model triage) for j-rig's functional layer (IEP is bandwidth-gated; this is a real cost lever). Also deepsec INFO.md project-context injection ~= eval-spec context_hints recorded-data fixtures.

REFS: deepsec github.com/vercel-labs/deepsec; convergence umbrella intent-eval-lab#4 (IEL-CONV-1) / Plane LAB-6; audit-harness emit-evidence + emit-snapshot-currency.py pattern; Blueprint B gate-result/v1 normative spec; DR-010 Q3.

description: Operationalizes the non-normative research in intent-eval-lab/000-docs/099-RR-eval-research/100-RR-LAND (meta_skill + 13-tool gap analysis). title: Decide j-rig CISO Gate G-1 scope: extend to OTel/log-file leaks or narrow docstring to stdout/stderr
description:
Child of bd_000-projects-rwr0 (umbrella review 2026-06-14). DECISION NEEDED (CSO/ISEDC).

Verified P1: packages/core/src/providers/ciso-gates/g1-credential-redaction.ts only intercepts process.stdout/stderr.write, but its docstring + normative PB-7 §6 require capturing OTel telemetry and local log files too. An adapter that leaks a credential via an OTel span attribute or fs.appendFileSync while keeping stdout/stderr clean PASSES G-1 — and G-1 is the disqualification gate that SELECTS which provider adapter ships. So a credential-leaking adapter can qualify.

This is a CSO call because it changes which adapter qualifies. OPTIONS: (a) narrow the docstring/reasons to truthfully scope G-1 to stdout/stderr and route OTel/log-file leak detection to a SEPARATE gate; (b) extend the harness to tee fs writes (writeFileSync/appendFileSync/createWriteStream) in a sandboxed temp dir + route OTel export through an in-memory span recorder that is also grepped. (a) is honest+cheap; (b) is more complete but heavier and may reshuffle adapter qualification.
close_reason: Resolved + shipped: j-rig PR #119 merged (3a70dbc9). Acting-CTO call = make the implementation honor the PB-7 §6 contract (no docstring-narrowing shortcut). CISO Gate G-1 now captures credential leaks via fs/log-file writes (writeFileSync/appendFileSync/createWriteStream/promises) AND OTel spans (added @opentelemetry/api+sdk-trace-base; in-memory recorder via ProxyTracerProvider.setDelegate), restored-in-finally, truthful docstring + reason strings. 10 leak-detection tests proven fail-without/pass-with; coverage gate green. title: Authorize iec AJV/Zod minLength parity fix: v2 STRICT-fork tightening or DR-049 freeze carve-out
description:
Child of bd_000-projects-rwr0 (umbrella review 2026-06-14). DECISION NEEDED (acting-CTO/ISEDC).

Verified P1: the Zod authoring validators check type only, never minLength:1, while the composed JSON Schema (AJV) enforces minLength:1 on description (upstream-base) + author/license/compatibility (is-overlay). So {description:''} etc. pass Zod but AJV rejects — an AJV<->Zod fold-agreement gap present in all 6 authoring contracts.

The fix is BUILT and correct (codegen-authoring.ts emits a non-empty check for any minLength>=1 string field; regen produced exactly the intended diff; fold-agreement test added). BUT it cannot ship to v1: src/__tests__/authoring-v1-frozen.test.ts machine-enforces the v1 authoring family is BYTE-FROZEN at v0.4.1 (DR-049/CTO settlement — 'v1 accepts every 0.4.1 artifact forever; tightenings go only to the STRICT v2 fork'). Adding a minLength rejection is a tightening the freeze forbids.

OPTIONS: (a) apply the tightening in the v2 STRICT-fork (copy-then-tighten — the sanctioned path); (b) an explicit DR-049 freeze carve-out for parity-only fixes. Both are architectural/governance calls, not autonomous. Interim mitigation already noted: a CONSUMERS.md note that INV-ENV-DISJOINT + minLength are Zod-only so AJV-only consumers (CCP Python validator) are aware.
close_reason: Resolved + shipped: intent-eval-core PR #51 merged (e29f071a). Acting-CTO call = v2 STRICT-fork (not a v1 freeze carve-out). The v2 schemas already enforced minLength:1; the gap was the codegen-generated v2 Zod checking type-only — now mirrors the schema floor on description/author/license/compatibility so v2 Zod<->AJV agree. v1 byte-freeze intact (1157+ tests, freeze guard + codegen idempotency green). CONSUMERS.md documents the one intentional Zod-only invariant (INV-ENV-DISJOINT) for AJV-only consumers. Found by the 2026-06-14 umbrella review.

title: Persist a per-repo last-known-good ingest snapshot so partial manifest-fetch failures don't regress live labs rows
description: Follow-up from the 2026-06-08 cron incident (run 27123737379): a transient manifest-fetch blackout made the cron render all-no-data and regress labs 4/6 -> 0/6. Mitigated by the blackout-guard in regenerate.yml (PR dashboard#26): if 0 repos verify, retry once then SKIP commit/deploy so the prior good deploy stays live. LIMITATION: the guard only catches TOTAL blackouts (0 verified). A PARTIAL fetch failure (e.g., 2 of 4 verify) still proceeds and regresses the unfetched rows to no-data, because .ingest-store is ephemeral per cron run (no persisted last-known-good). COMPLETE FIX: persist verified per-repo snapshots across cron runs (GitHub Actions cache or committed store) and have ingest-render fall back to a repo's prior VERIFIED snapshot + a stale_since badge on a fetch miss (the DR-035 last-known-good design) instead of rendering it no-data. Also consider authenticating the manifest fetch (raise the unauthenticated GitHub rate limit) + fetch retry/backoff. Verify: simulate a single-repo fetch failure and confirm that repo renders stale (not no-data) while the others stay live.
notes: Mirror: dashboard#17. Discovered during 'verify the daily cron runs clean' on 2026-06-08; parent of the nr75.10 cron work.
close_reason: COMPLETE FIX shipped + verified end-to-end on PR #27 (intent-eval-dashboard, branch feat/nr75-partial-fetch-lkg, required CI green). regenerate.yml now persists .ingest-store/ across cron runs via actions/cache (restore-before-ingest + save-always, immutable per-run key + restore-keys fallback) so the already-correct renderer (buildRenderInput keeps prior snapshot + staleSince) serves each failed repo's prior-good snapshot on a PARTIAL fetch miss instead of regressing it to no-data; a row only goes no-data if it has NEVER verified. Also removed the blackout-retry rm -rf .ingest-store that would have destroyed restored prior-good (stores are content-addressed + idempotent). Proof: src/ingest/partial-fetch-lkg.test.ts — two-pass test against real FS stores + runLivePass + renderer + testing view-model asserts a fetched-then-missed repo renders stale (real rows) not no-data, while a never-verified repo is no-data; companion case proves the ephemeral-store regression this fixes. Full pnpm run check green (393 tests), harness-hash OK, zero new deps. Use bd-sync close bd_000-projects-nr75.17 --also-close-gh to mirror (note: GH umbrella #17 covers the broader epic — PR used Refs #17, do NOT close #17). (PR #https://github.com/jeremylongshore/intent-eval-dashboard/pull/27 merged 8ebc77b5a235aa5956acb3a110e7b87bbb13a1a6, 2026-06-13)

description:
VISION (Jeremy 2026-06-07): any report generated by any repo in the IEP ecosystem should have its own section on labs.intentsolutions.io that you can just open in a browser as HTML. Today these reports are generated locally/CI and thrown away or gitignored (j-rig reports/crap CRAP scores, intent-eval-dashboard reports/arch, intent-audit-harness gate outputs, intent-eval-lab research/phase-a-0 eval results, coverage reports across all repos). Make them a first-class, web-viewable, per-repo surface.

GROUNDING (current dashboard architecture): intent-eval-dashboard is the labs.intentsolutions.io surface (6th platform repo, DR-035 ISEDC Session 8). TS/pnpm; it already ingests + renders eval-sets + signed Evidence Bundles via site/ + site-internal/ + ingest/ + data/ + reports/ with deploy.yml + ingest-ci.yml + regenerate.yml. It ALREADY has the ingest→render→deploy spine for eval-sets; this epic GENERALIZES that spine to arbitrary report types from every repo.

DESIGN SKETCH (to refine in a DR):
1. Report taxonomy — enumerate report types + producers: CRAP (audit-harness/j-rig), coverage (all TS repos), gate-result/v1 (audit-harness, kernel-defined), eval-set results (j-rig, lab Phase A.0), architecture (audit-harness arch-check), mutation (where present), audit reports (TEST_AUDIT etc.).
2. Transport — how each repo's CI gets reports to the dashboard: upload as CI artifact + dashboard ingest pulls, OR repos push to a data branch/dir the dashboard reads. Reuse existing ingest-ci.yml pattern; standardize an output shape (gate-result/v1 already canonical for gate rows).
3. Rendering — HTML per report type (CSV like crap → tables; eval results → scorecards; coverage → summary). Per-repo section: labs.intentsolutions.io/reports/<repo>/<report-type>/.
4. Access — public vs tailnet-internal split (dashboard already has site/ public + site-internal/); some reports internal-only.

HARD CONSTRAINT (CISO binding): labs.intentsolutions.io may host blog/methodology/REPORTS content but NEVER an in-toto predicate URI, OTel attribute namespace, or attestation predicate identifier — those live ONLY at evals.intentsolutions.io. The reports hub is content rendering; keep predicate/attestation identifiers off labs.

RELATED: existing dashboard eval-set browser (the prototype of this pattern); bd_000-projects-ktm0 (dogfood Claude Code OTel — telemetry is another report/signal source for the hub); bd_000-projects-fzdr (real Claude-session data). title: Benchmark gbrain on the public Evidence Bench via a citation-integrity eval (signed, free-tier, non-derivative)
description:
Move 2 of the snoopy-fluttering-comet plan, RE-SCOPED after 2026-06-01 feasibility investigation. Supersedes the original tr08.5/tr08.7 framing (which wrongly assumed gbrain is an LLM you run the SKILL.md-editing eval against).

KEY FINDINGS (2026-06-01):
- gbrain (github.com/garrytan/gbrain) is a MEMORY system, not an LLM. Interfaces: CLI (gbrain capture / search / think / graph-query), MCP server, TS library. 'gbrain think' returns a synthesized answer WITH citations.
- Running the Phase A.0 SKILL.md-editing eval against gbrain would be nonsense (grading a librarian on writing code). The honest, NON-DERIVATIVE benchmark = a CITATION-INTEGRITY eval: feed gbrain a known doc corpus, ask questions via 'gbrain think', score whether every claim traces to a real captured source (vs hallucinated citations). Provenance is IS's differentiated lane; gbrain-evals measures retrieval P@K/R@K, NOT citation integrity. Avoids the 'gbrain-evals but signed' trap (ground-truth review HIGH-risk item).
- COST: free. bun 1.2.23 installed. gbrain rides free NVIDIA NIM for BOTH embeddings (nvidia/nv-embedqa-e5-v5 at integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/embeddings, OpenAI-compatible) AND 'think' synthesis (Groq or NVIDIA NIM). UNCONFIRMED: exact gbrain env var to override embedding base URL (docs reference docs/integrations/embedding-providers.md; 16 recipes incl OpenAI-compatible) — 5-min repo check, not a blocker.
- Keys: not in env; Phase A.0 exported NVIDIA_API_KEY at runtime (nvapi- prefix, free dev tier, 40 req/min). Same pattern here.

STATUS: DEFERRED. Per Jeremy 2026-06-01 — finish all other open wedge beads first, then return to this deliberately. Pre-registered DESIGN doc comes before any code (mirrors Phase A.0 discipline).

title: Research and standardize a bead naming convention that aligns with gastownhall/beads upstream and works as a global IS standard across ICOS, QMD, IEP, and future knowledge bases
description:
Investigate the right naming methodology for bd work items so it (a) aligns with the prescribed gastownhall/beads upstream convention to ease future ecosystem integration, (b) usable as a global IS standard across multiple knowledge bases (ICOS, QMD, IEP, partner-portals, future work), and (c) mirrors the abbreviation-coded discipline of /doc-filing's NNN-CC-ABCD-<title>-<date>.md standard.

## Why this matters
Current state: each repo has its own bd workspace prefix (bd_000-projects-, intentional-cognition-os-, qmd-team-intent-kb-, etc.). Titles are plain English per the IS umbrella CLAUDE.md SOP. Labels are ad-hoc topic words. System IDs are 3-char autogen.

Problems with the status quo:
1. Cross-knowledge-base queries are awkward — no shared vocabulary
2. If we ever want to integrate into the larger gastownhall/beads ecosystem (multi-org, shared registry, etc.), our ad-hoc naming will clash
3. /doc-filing has been transformative for doc organization because the CC-ABCD codes are mnemonic + greppable + sortable. Bead naming has no equivalent.
4. ICOS and QMD knowledge work would benefit from shared classifiers (e.g., RESEARCH, IMPL, AUDIT, DECISION, REFINE etc.) the way docs benefit from RR/PP/AA/AT/DR.

## Hard non-goals (this epic)
- NOT making any changes yet — investigation only
- NOT modifying existing beads
- NOT picking a winner before research lands

## Methodology
1. Read gastownhall/beads upstream docs for prescribed naming + ID conventions
2. Survey other bd ecosystem users for de-facto conventions
3. Catalogue IS internal conventions in use (umbrella CLAUDE.md + per-project CLAUDE.md files + bd workspace configs across ICOS, QMD, IEP)
4. Compare to /doc-filing standard structure (categorical codes + chronological numbering + date suffix)
5. Propose 1-3 candidate global-IS conventions; surface tradeoffs
6. ISEDC ratification of a single global standard
7. Migration plan (if standard differs materially from status quo)

## Decision shape
Output: an ISEDC-ratified AT-DECR in some appropriate home (likely intent-eval-lab/000-docs/ or a new central IS standards location) defining:
- The bead title convention (when to use plain English; when to use categorical codes)
- The bd workspace prefix convention (per-project? shared? hybrid?)
- The label taxonomy (controlled vocabulary vs free-form)
- Cross-knowledge-base mapping (how a bead at ICOS references work at IEP)
- Migration policy for existing beads (retroactive rename vs grandfather-and-go-forward)

Reference precedent: the IS bead naming SOP in umbrella CLAUDE.md (plain-English-only rule from 2026-05-22) was a deliberate choice — this research either reinforces that choice with a richer extension, OR proposes a successor.

## Connected work
- Sibling epic bd_000-projects-2h15 (SkillSpector research) — both are landscape-survey epics; outputs may inform each other
- /doc-filing standard at ~/000-projects/002-command-bible/DOCUMENT-FILING-STANDARD-v3.0.md — the precedent abbreviation-coded discipline this epic asks 'should we extend to beads'

title: Research NVIDIA SkillSpector and the surrounding AI-skill-evaluation landscape to decide whether to adopt, fork, integrate, or build-vs
description:
Decide whether IEP should adopt, fork, integrate, or build-vs against NVIDIA's SkillSpector (github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) + the surrounding skill-evaluation landscape.

## Why
The Intent Eval Platform's flagship eval-set is the j-rig 7-layer binary-criteria skill evaluation. The Skill Refiner buildout (Phase A.0 currently in flight per bd_000-projects-214c.8) depends on having a defensible eval surface. NVIDIA shipping SkillSpector raises four orthogonal questions:

1. **Adopt** — does SkillSpector cover what j-rig covers, well enough that we should adopt it as the upstream + retire j-rig?
2. **Fork** — does it cover most of j-rig but with a path-divergence we'd want to make IS-canonical?
3. **Integrate** — does it solve a complementary problem (e.g., specific evaluation primitives we can compose) without conflicting with j-rig's 7-layer thesis?
4. **Build-vs** — does it solve a different problem entirely (perhaps with NVIDIA-specific assumptions) such that the right move is to continue j-rig + reference SkillSpector as related-work-context only?

## Methodology
Survey SkillSpector itself + the broader landscape (Anthropic Evals Hub, OpenAI Evals, HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard, lm-evaluation-harness, METR public reports, Apollo, Redwood Research, AI2 Tülu's eval mechanisms). Compare against j-rig binary-eval 7-layer + the planned IEP Evidence Bundle architecture (DR-010 unification thesis + DR-035 dashboard binding).

## Decision shape
Produce a Decision Record under intent-eval-lab/000-docs/ with the four-way choice ratified by relevant ISEDC seats (likely CTO + CSO for adopt-vs-fork; CMO + VP DevRel for community-signal implications; CFO for bandwidth allocation). If 'integrate' or 'build-vs' wins, the j-rig + IEP-dashboard architecture stays as-is. If 'adopt' wins, this becomes a substantial pivot.

## Hard non-goals
- Not implementing SkillSpector adoption in this epic — that's a follow-on if the decision lands that way
- Not blocking Phase A.0 — A.0 finishes per current plan regardless of this research's outcome
- Not surveying every adjacent project exhaustively — scope to projects with material overlap with j-rig's specific thesis (binary per-layer findings, not aggregate scores)
close_reason: DR-037 ratified outcome INTEGRATE. Closes the research epic; the optional audit-harness CI integration becomes a P3 follow-up bead (filed when user-pull signal emerges).

title: Convert bd<->GH<->Plane from three-way sync to canonical-bd + computed projections (design spike)
description:
Per IEP thinker-panel review (convergent: Hickey #2 most-costly, Cunningham #3, Kleppmann #3, 2026-05-25). The three-layer mirror is the canonical place-oriented-programming anti-pattern in the workflow — three places, each holding 'the same' mutable thing, papered over with bd-sync.

Hickey: 'Pick one canonical store. Beads is already the source of truth — make GH and Plane projections of beads, not peer copies. A projection is computed, not synced. The bd issues.jsonl is the VALUE; GH and Plane are VIEWS derived from it via one-way export.'

Cunningham: 'wiki philosophy: pick ONE place to think, link everything else to it. Today they're three databases pretending to be one.'

Kleppmann: 'classic dual-write problem (DDIA Ch. 11). The throttle-bypass incident (DR-022) confirmed: when you have to add a gate to verify-before-asserting, your model has lost place-vs-identity distinctness.'

Action (design spike, NOT implementation): 
1. Map current write paths in bd, gh, plane — what mutates each layer? 
2. Identify which mutations would lose semantics if downgraded to projection (the answer: human comments on GH/Plane).
3. Decide: ingress-only on those layers + computed-output from bd, OR genuine canonical inversion.
4. Cost the migration: number of CI integrations, scripts, conventions that assume the current model.
5. Produce DR with recommendation; ratify via ISEDC if substantive.

Recovery cost compounds daily; recommend pulling forward.

title: iah-crap-score-dot-dir-asymmetry — score_python excludes all dot-dirs but main() input-hash walk only excludes named dot-dirs
description:
Surfaced by Gemini on intent-eval-lab PR #72 (line 406 of vendored crap-score.py). Companion bug to niv8 (closed in v1.1.4): SAME asymmetry class but different dimension.

In score_python() (line ~99-103):

    scanned = [
        p.name for p in root.iterdir()
        if p.is_dir()
        and not p.name.startswith('.')    # excludes ALL dot-dirs
        and p.name not in EXCLUDED_DIRS
        and p.name not in test_dirs
        and any(p.rglob('*.py'))
    ]

In main() --json input-hash block (line ~405):

    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in EXCLUDED_DIRS]
        # ← only excludes dot-dirs explicitly listed in EXCLUDED_DIRS
        # (.git, .venv, .tox, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, .next, .nuxt, .cache)
        # All OTHER dot-dirs (.github, .vscode, .husky, .devcontainer, .idea,
        # .circleci, .gitlab, .clinerules, .claude, etc.) traversed normally.

Effect: a repo with .github/scripts/*.py (common pattern for Actions custom code), or .husky/_/*.py hooks, etc., gets those files hashed in input_hash but NOT scanned as candidates by score_python. Input_hash diverges from what the user would expect given the score_python coverage.

Fix: extend main's dirs[:] filter to also exclude dot-prefix dirs:

    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in EXCLUDED_DIRS and not d.startswith('.')]

OR factor out a shared filter function that both call sites use. Either way the invariant is: 'main and score_python see the SAME set of directories.'

Verification: deliberate-failure test — create a temp dir with a .github/foo.py file, run crap-score --json before+after fix, observe that .github/foo.py was previously included in input_hash but is now excluded (matching score_python's behavior).

Acceptance: both call sites filter dot-prefix dirs identically; deliberate test passes; ruff still clean. Patch-level release (v1.1.5).

Companion to (or bundle target of) iah-python-wrapper-scripts-sync (65k4) if architecturally feasible.
close_reason: crap-score dot-dir walk asymmetry fixed (score walk + input-hash walk now exclude the same set) (PR #69 merged 4c42f57e2d3e4449b01269e625ae713441e8db4a, 2026-06-18)

title: iah-crap-score-exclusion-dedup — score_python ignore set + main prune set are duplicated AND inconsistent
description:
Surfaced by Gemini on intent-eval-lab PR #71 (line 88 of vendored crap-score.py).

Current state of scripts/crap-score.py:

score_python() defines (was reformatted in v1.1.3 to multi-line):

    ignore = {
        '.git', '.venv', 'venv', 'node_modules', 'dist', 'build', 'target',
        '.tox', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache', 'reports', '__pycache__',
    }

main() (the --json input-hash block, added in v1.1.1) defines:

    prune = {'.git', 'node_modules', '.venv', 'venv', '__pycache__', 'dist', 'build',
             'target', '.tox', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache', '.next', '.nuxt', '.cache'}

Two sets, two names, same intent (skip-during-walk), divergent contents:
- ignore has 'reports' but lacks .next, .nuxt, .cache
- prune has .next, .nuxt, .cache but lacks 'reports'

Net effect: a repo with a reports/ directory will be correctly skipped by score_python's candidate scan but the --json input-hash walk WILL descend into reports/ and hash any .py files there. A repo with .next/.nuxt/.cache dirs (modern web frameworks) hits the opposite asymmetry: score_python's candidate scan could include them, while the input-hash walk correctly prunes.

Fix: extract a module-level constant EXCLUDED_DIRS (or similar name) and use in BOTH score_python's candidate-discovery AND main's --json input-hash walk. Sets should be byte-equivalent.

Suggested union as starting point (preserves both):
    EXCLUDED_DIRS = {
        '.git', '.venv', 'venv', 'node_modules', '__pycache__',
        'dist', 'build', 'target', '.tox', '.mypy_cache', '.pytest_cache',
        '.next', '.nuxt', '.cache', 'reports',
    }

Acceptance: single module-level constant; both call sites reference it; ruff still clean; deliberate-failure test (add a .py file under reports/ and another under .next/, run crap-score --json, observe both excluded from input-hash).

Bundle with iah-gherkin-prev-blank-noise (o9q1) + iah-gherkin-single-awk-opt (vawm) + iah-python-wrapper-scripts-sync (65k4, if architecturally feasible same PR) into audit-harness v1.1.4.
close_reason: Closed by audit-harness PR #40 merged 2026-05-25 (squash commit b4f855c2, tag v1.1.4 pushed). scripts/crap-score.py had two separate exclusion sets (ignore in score_python, prune in main --json input-hash block) with divergent contents — ignore had 'reports' but lacked .next/.nuxt/.cache; prune had the modern web-framework dirs but lacked 'reports'. Asymmetric coverage was a real latent bug (repo with reports/ would skip score_python's candidate scan but its .py files DID get hashed by the input-hash walk). Fixed by extracting module-level EXCLUDED_DIRS constant (union of both prior sets, 15 entries) referenced from both call sites. Single source of truth; invariant documented at the constant's definition. AAR: 009-AA-AACR-v1.1.4-cleanup-bundle-2026-05-25.md § 2.3.

title: iah-python-wrapper-scripts-sync — Python + Rust wrapper packages bundle stale scripts/ mirrors of canonical sources
description:
Surfaced during P6 Phase A2 ruff rollout (audit-harness v1.1.3 PR). The Python wrapper at python/src/intent_audit_harness/scripts/crap-score.py and the Rust wrapper at rust/scripts/crap-score.py are STALE MIRRORS of the canonical scripts/crap-score.py, ~1 month behind (as of 2026-05-24). Missing:

- v1.1.1 --json envelope emission (the entire if args.json: block)
- v1.1.1 which_or_none('go') PATH guard (silent crash on Go-less systems)
- v1.1.1 rglob → os.walk pruning (perf on large repos)

Users who 'pip install intent-audit-harness && audit-harness crap' get the OLDER script, not what the npm-published @intentsolutions/audit-harness ships. Same likely for 'cargo install intent-audit-harness'.

Three resolution paths:
(a) Build-time copy in pyproject.toml + Cargo.toml: hatch + cargo run a pre-build step that copies scripts/* into the wrapper packages. Cleanest; no manual sync.
(b) Symlinks: python/src/intent_audit_harness/scripts → ../../../scripts. Simple but symlinks don't always survive tarball packaging well.
(c) Hand-sync with CI check: a CI job diffs the mirrors against canonical and fails on drift. Manual but auditable.

Current workaround: ruff.toml excludes the mirrors from lint (extend-exclude includes 'python/src/intent_audit_harness/scripts/' + 'rust/scripts/'). Exclusion drops once the sync mechanism ships.

Acceptance: pip install of intent-audit-harness from current main + 'audit-harness crap --json' produces the same envelope output as the canonical npm package. Same for Rust crate. CI gate detects future drift.

Drift-guard scripts/check-wrapper-sync.sh added (reds on drift exit 1, --fix repairs — both proven) and wired as the ci.yml wrapper-sync CI lane so this can never recur silently. Obsolete ruff mirror-dir exclusions dropped; .harness-hash re-pinned for the new script (20->21, only new line). ruff/shellcheck/py_compile clean, crap-score 6/6 + golden 2/2 + harness-hash --verify OK. title: iah-gherkin-prev-blank-noise — gherkin-lint.sh prev_blank=1 triggers awk default print, floods output with every feature-file line
description:
Surfaced by Gemini on intent-eval-lab PR #70 (line 119 of vendored gherkin-lint.sh). Pre-existing bug confirmed in audit-harness v1.1.2 AAR § 5 as deferred scope; Gemini's repeat-flag escalates priority.

Root cause: scripts/gherkin-lint.sh third awk block (the And-at-scenario-start checker) opens with:

    prev_blank = 1                                            # bare expression at top-level
    /^[[:space:]]*$/ { prev_blank = 1; next }                # blank-line handler
    /^[[:space:]]*Scenario/ { in_scenario = 1; ... ; next }
    /^[[:space:]]*(Given|When|Then|And|But)/ { ... }

The bare 'prev_blank = 1' at line 1 of the awk script is interpreted by awk as a pattern (an expression that evaluates to 1 = true on every line). Patterns without explicit actions get awk's default action: { print }. So every input line gets printed to stdout.

Compounding: prev_blank is never USED anywhere in this awk script — the assignment serves no purpose. Both lines that touch it (the top-level expression + the assignment inside the blank-line pattern) can be removed entirely.

Fix: delete both 'prev_blank = 1' references in the third awk block of scripts/gherkin-lint.sh. Output becomes clean (only WARN/ERROR lines from intentional printf statements).

Verification: re-run the deliberate-failure test from v1.1.2 AAR § 2 (a feature with 'Scenario: ... \n And ...'). Pre-fix output includes the full feature-file content interleaved with the ERROR line. Post-fix output contains ONLY 'gherkin-lint: falling back to awk rubric...' header + the ERROR line + summary + exit.

Patch-level release. Pair with iah-gherkin-single-awk-opt (other Gemini PR #70 finding) for a single audit-harness v1.1.3 PR.
close_reason: Closed by audit-harness PR #40 merged 2026-05-25 (squash commit b4f855c2, tag v1.1.4 pushed). Bare 'prev_blank = 1' at top of 3rd awk block in scripts/gherkin-lint.sh was an always-true awk pattern triggering default { print } action; flooded stdout with every feature-file line. prev_blank had zero call sites (verified via grep -n). Both touches deleted. Output-noise reduction verified end-to-end via deliberate-failure test: pre-fix output included the full feature file interleaved with the ERROR line; post-fix output contains only the ERROR line. AAR: 009-AA-AACR-v1.1.4-cleanup-bundle-2026-05-25.md § 2.1.

title: iah-script-robustness-upstream — 6 robustness/portability fixes to audit-harness scripts surfaced by Gemini on intent-eval-lab PR #67
description:
Gemini code review on intent-eval-lab PR #67 (harness-hash rollout, which vendors audit-harness@846ff6a as a snapshot) surfaced 6 medium-severity findings in the audit-harness scripts themselves. The lab PR is mergeable as-is — these are upstream improvements, not lab-side defects. Each fix lands in audit-harness via its own PR; downstream consumers (lab + j-rig + future) get the improvements when they re-vendor or re-install.

Findings (all rated medium by Gemini):

1. **escape-scan.sh:55** — mktemp temp files (DIFF_SRC for --staged + --range modes) leak. Add `trap rm -f "$DIFF_SRC" EXIT` to clean up on exit. Especially relevant when run as a local git hook.

2. **crap-score.py:176** — `go test -coverprofile=...` runs without checking if `go` is in PATH. Crashes with FileNotFoundError on systems without Go. Add `which_or_none("go")` guard matching the existing pattern for `radon` and `gocyclo`.

3. **crap-score.py:392** — `root.rglob("*")` traverses every directory including `node_modules`, `.venv`, `.git`. Use `os.walk` with `dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in (".git", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv")]` to prune unwanted directories. Performance win on large repos.

4. **emit-evidence.sh:106** — `python3 -c "...json.load(open(\"$PKG_JSON\"))..."` directly interpolates the shell variable into the Python source. Path with special characters (single quote) breaks. Fix: pass via argv — `python3 -c "import json, sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])))" "$PKG_JSON"`.

5. **bias-count.sh:39** — `find ... -exec sha256sum {} \;` spawns one sha256sum process per file. Use `-exec sha256sum {} +` to batch. Performance win on large test suites.

6. **harness-hash.sh:102** — `sha256sum` is Linux/coreutils-only. macOS uses `shasum -a 256`. For cross-platform engineer-local use, wrap with detection: `if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then SHA256=sha256sum; else SHA256="shasum -a 256"; fi`.

None of these are blocking for any current CI gate (audit-harness self CI runs on Ubuntu only). Filed as a single follow-on bead under iep-P3-audit-harness-hardening cluster.

When fixed, audit-harness gets a SemVer minor bump (additive robustness improvements; no API change). Downstream consumers re-vendor or re-install via `AUDIT_HARNESS_VERSION=vX.Y.Z curl ... | bash`.
close_reason: Closed by audit-harness PR #37 (v1.1.1) — 6 Gemini findings fixed at source; lab PR #67 re-vendored. AAR audit-harness/000-docs/006.

title: Research: trace-driven skill evolution as Evidence Bundle consumer — design + references
description:
Open question: how does the Intent Eval Platform consume agent-curated skill evolution? Self-improving skill ecosystems (the agentskills.io open-standard pattern) generate streams of skill diffs (new skills + patches to existing ones) at runtime; without a guardrail layer those diffs cannot be trusted.

This issue scopes the **research + design surface** before any code lands. The eval platform is uniquely positioned to be the trust layer: audit-harness gates the diff statically, j-rig-binary-eval scores the variant against baseline behaviorally, intent-rollout-gate signs the ship/no-ship decision.

## What we're studying

1. **Trace format** — can an Evidence Bundle (v0.1.0-draft) carry a skill-invocation trace? Inputs (user prompt, tool calls, final state) + outputs (skill diff, success signal). May need a new bundle subject type `skill-variant`.
2. **Variant generator** — out of scope for the platform. We consume diffs from any producer (a runtime agent, a DSPy/GEPA-style optimizer, a human author). Producer-agnostic by design.
3. **Guardrail stack composition:**
   - **audit-harness:** new gate `skill-diff-safety` (size limit, no escape patterns, no cache-busting frontmatter changes, hash-pin compatibility, semantic-preservation heuristic)
   - **j-rig-binary-eval:** existing 7-layer rubric runs against (baseline skill vs. variant skill) producing 14 yes/no signals
   - **intent-rollout-gate:** GHA action reads bundle, applies repo policy (e.g., "variant must pass all 7 layers AND not regress any baseline layer AND have human approval")
4. **Signature surface** — what does the in-toto Statement attest? Subject = skill-variant content hash; predicate = bundle URI.

## References for examples

- **agentskills.io open standard** — vendor-neutral skill format spec; the format every agent runtime is converging on
- **DSPy + GEPA** (ICLR 2026) — example of a trace-driven optimizer that proposes variants from execution traces (this is the kind of *producer* the eval platform would consume from); 5-guardrail pattern (test suite + size + cache compat + semantic preservation + human review) is the relevant prior art
- **Our existing j-rig-binary-eval/PRD.md** — the 7-layer binary rubric is already designed for skill grading
- **Our existing audit-harness scripts/** — escape-scan, harness-hash, bias-count are reusable
- **Evidence Bundle v0.1.0-draft schema** (this repo: specs/evidence-bundle/) — would need extension for skill-variant subjects
- **Cross-ref CCP beads:** claude-nwdy (progressive disclosure), claude-22cg (conditional visibility), and the env-var-self-decl bead — those define the skill format the platform evaluates

## Acceptance (research phase)

- specs/skill-evolution/v0.1.0-draft/RESEARCH.md authored — scope, prior art, non-goals, decision points
- Decision: does Evidence Bundle v0.1.0 need a new subject type or can skill-variant fit under the existing subject schema? (Documented either way.)
- specs/skill-evolution/v0.1.0-draft/SPEC-DRAFT.md authored — at most a sketch; ships behind 'draft' label
- One concrete worked example: a hand-authored skill diff (before/after SKILL.md) walked through all three eval-platform layers, with the resulting Evidence Bundle JSON committed under tests/fixtures/skill-variant-example/

## Non-goals

- Building a variant generator. Producer-agnostic by design.
- Wiring this into CCP today. Skill format work in CCP (claude-nwdy, claude-22cg, env-var-self-decl bead) is prerequisite for any eval to make sense.
- Production rollout. This is research phase only.

title: Investigate dogfooding Claude Code's native OTel telemetry from real sessions as an IEP observability + eval data source
description:
Idea (from Jeremy 2026-06-07): we publish OTel signal conventions for the eval platform but may not be consuming our OWN OTel data. Claude Code emits native OpenTelemetry (metrics + logs/events via OTEL_* / CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY env: token usage, tool calls, session/cost, model). Jeremy runs many Claude Code sessions daily — that's a live, real-usage telemetry stream we are NOT currently ingesting.

THE FOLLOW-UP: figure out whether/how to dogfood that telemetry — pipe Jeremy's real Claude Code session OTel into the IEP observability + eval substrate. Two payoffs: (1) self-instrumentation proof ('we run on our own signals'), (2) a real-usage data source for evals/landscape rather than synthetic prompts.

CONTEXT / RELATED WORK (do not duplicate — connect):
- Lab OTel RFC draft: intent-eval-lab/000-docs/001-DR-RFC-otel-agent-rollout-gate-signals-draft.md (proposes agent.rollout.gate.* + agent.evidence_bundle.* conventions; NOT yet filed).
- OTel emit/pin beads: 9pi3 (pin OTel semconv before kernel v0.2.0), fis (iah-E07 OTel instrumentation), mm0i (iah-E07d attr schema), vb9e (iaj-E08d alignment). Those are about US EMITTING OTel; this bead is about US CONSUMING Claude Code's OTel.
- Existing dogfood cluster iar-E10a..d dogfoods the ROLLOUT-GATE on repos — different axis from ingesting Claude session telemetry.
- Adjacent angle: fzdr (0xSero/ai-data-extraction) extracts Claude/Cursor session HISTORIES from local storage; this bead is the live-OTel-stream complement. Decide if they converge into one 'real Claude-session data' ingestion seam.

OPEN QUESTIONS: where does the OTel land (Netdata/collector on the VPS? a dedicated collector?); privacy (session content vs metrics-only); does it feed the dashboard, an eval corpus, or both; is there a canonical 'self-usage' eval-set.
acceptance_criteria: A written finding + decision: whether to ingest Claude Code OTel, the collector/sink design, the privacy posture (metrics-only vs content), and whether it converges with fzdr into one real-session ingestion seam. If GO, spin out implementation beads under the right repo (likely iah/iel).

title: Investigate 0xSero/ai-data-extraction as a real-agent-interaction data source for IEP evals, and assess the tools/testing-platforms that surround it
description:
Repo: https://github.com/0xSero/ai-data-extraction (Python 3.6+, stdlib-only, MIT, ~730 stars / 75 forks, last active Jan 2025, 'Production Ready', 7 open PRs).

WHAT IT IS: a toolkit that extracts conversation histories + code context + metadata from 8+ AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Trae, Continue, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) into standardized JSONL. Handles version-specific local storage (SQLite, JSONL, proprietary KV) across macOS/Linux/Windows. Captures rich metadata: timestamps, model names, file paths, line ranges, suggested-diff/edit histories, multi-file context.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER TO US (the angle to investigate):
- Real-agent-interaction data as an eval SUBSTRATE: could seed j-rig / Phase A.0-style eval corpora, ground-truth, and behavioral-eval fixtures from actual Claude Code / Cursor sessions rather than synthetic prompts.
- Multi-tool aggregation + standardized schema lines up with the Evidence Bundle 'one schema, many emitters' thesis — is the extracted JSONL a candidate input shape, or does it map onto an EvalTarget/corpus entity?
- Landscape value: the user explicitly wants to understand 'the tools and testing platforms / evals that surround it' — i.e. who else consumes this kind of agent-session data, and where IEP sits competitively.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
1) License fit — it's MIT; IEP ecosystem is Apache-2.0. Vendoring vs. referencing vs. reimplementing the extraction idea.
2) Privacy/sanitization — extracted data can contain proprietary/sensitive code; what guardrails before any eval-corpus use.
3) API-less / local-only extraction — implications for reproducible CI-driven eval pipelines.
4) Does it inform a new corpus-ingestion seam in j-rig or the lab, or is it purely reference/landscape?
5) Map adjacent tools/testing platforms in the same space for a landscape note (possible CONTENT blog idea).
acceptance_criteria: A short written finding (lab 000-docs RR-LAND or a note) that: states whether/how the toolkit (or its approach) is useful to IEP evals; resolves the license + privacy questions; recommends adopt / reference-only / pass; and sketches the surrounding tools/testing-platform landscape.

title: DEFERRED: Skill Refiner MLOps — drift policy (weekly re-validation; event-triggered on upstream model bump; auto-refine on persistent drift)
description: Phase F MLOps. Trigger: first observed drift incident in production OR ≥100 active SkillVersion records. Weekly re-validation of stable-tier skills via cron + J-Rig Binary Eval. Event-triggered re-validation on upstream model version bumps. Auto-re-refinement triggered on persistent drift signal (N consecutive weeks score degraded). Cost dashboard via OTel spans. Plan ref: 025 § 4 Phase F.

title: DEFERRED: Skill Refiner MLOps — partner skill pins (partner pins SkillVersion ID; promotion proceeds per-partner)
description: Phase F MLOps. Trigger: ≥5 partners consume Refined skills AND first partner refuses a promotion. Partner config schema includes pinned SkillVersion ID per skill; promotion per-partner; decouples partner risk tolerance from platform-wide rollout cadence. Plan ref: 025 § 4 Phase F.

title: DEFERRED: Skill Refiner MLOps — canary rollouts (per-partner traffic routing of SkillVersions through shadow → canary-10 → canary-50 → 100 ladder)
description: Phase F MLOps. Trigger: ≥5 partners consume Refined skills. SkillVersion promotion graph: shadow → canary-10% → canary-50% → 100% → archived. DR per transition. Per-partner promotion (not lockstep). Plan ref: 025 § 4 Phase F.

title: DEFERRED: Skill Refiner MLOps — eval-set governance (versioned eval sets, quarterly review, rolling-production replacement, adversarial-append)
description: Phase F MLOps. Trigger: ≥5 partners consume Refined skills OR ≥100 SkillVersion records OR first drift incident. Scope: eval set versioning + change-log, quarterly review by acting CTO + CISO, rolling production replacement, adversarial-append. Plan ref: 025 § 4 Phase F.

title: DEFERRED: Skill Refiner creator sibling (would generate NEW skills from scratch) — gated on external evidence that self-generated skills can clear no-skill baseline
description: Deferred indefinitely per plan 025 § 2. Public benchmark evidence: self-generated skills underperform no-skill baseline. Re-open trigger: (a) external work demonstrates the bar can be cleared OR (b) partner explicitly asks AND accepts risk. Until then: no code, no design, no marketplace listing. Plan ref: 025 § 4 Phase D.

title: iah-shellcheck-version-pin — pin shellcheck version in audit-harness CI to avoid silent rule-set drift
description: P6 follow-up surfaced in v1.1.2 AAR § 5. CI currently does 'sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck' which pulls whatever Ubuntu 22.04 ships (currently 0.9.0). title: iah-gherkin-single-awk-opt — collapse process_awk_output() helper to single awk pass
description:
Surfaced by Gemini on intent-eval-lab PR #70 (line 67 of vendored gherkin-lint.sh). Optimization of the process_awk_output() helper introduced in audit-harness v1.1.2 (PR #38).

Current implementation (v1.1.2):

    process_awk_output() {
      local out="$1"
      [ -z "$out" ] && return 0
      local w e
      w=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/^WARN /{c++} END{print c+0}')
      e=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '/^ERROR /{c++} END{print c+0}')
      WARN_COUNT=$((WARN_COUNT + w))
      ERROR_COUNT=$((ERROR_COUNT + e))
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
    }

Forks 2 awk subprocesses per call (4 calls per feature file = 8 awk processes per file).

Gemini-suggested single-pass:

    process_awk_output() {
      local out="$1"
      [ -z "$out" ] && return 0
      local w=0 e=0
      read -r w e < <(awk '/^WARN /{w++} /^ERROR /{e++} END {print w+0, e+0}' <<< "$out")
      WARN_COUNT=$((WARN_COUNT + w))
      ERROR_COUNT=$((ERROR_COUNT + e))
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
    }

Halves the awk fork count. Microsecond-scale perf improvement on small features/ dirs; meaningful on large ones (hundreds of feature files).

Acceptance: applied, deliberate-failure test from v1.1.2 AAR still produces exit 1 + correct counts. Counter behavior byte-equivalent.

Pair with iah-gherkin-prev-blank-noise (Gemini's other PR #70 finding) for a single audit-harness v1.1.3 PR.
close_reason: Closed by audit-harness PR #40 merged 2026-05-25 (squash commit b4f855c2, tag v1.1.4 pushed). process_awk_output() helper in scripts/gherkin-lint.sh collapsed from 2 awk subprocesses per call (one counting WARN, one counting ERROR) to a single awk pass using read -r w e < <(awk '/^WARN /{w++} /^ERROR /{e++} END {print w+0, e+0}' <<< "$out") per Gemini PR #39 verbatim suggestion. Halves the awk fork count from 8 to 4 per feature file. Verified with mixed WARN+ERROR test: 2 WARNs + 1 ERROR feature → summary '2 warning(s), 1 error(s)', exit 1. AAR: 009-AA-AACR-v1.1.4-cleanup-bundle-2026-05-25.md § 2.2.

title: iah-cargo-lock-tracking — decide whether to commit rust/Cargo.lock or document its gitignored status
description:
Follow-up from v1.1.1 (PR #37 / bd_000-projects-qqkq) AAR § 4.

Discovered during v1.1.1 work: rust/Cargo.lock is gitignored. The local file was at 1.0.2 while the rest of the manifests are at 1.1.0 (now 1.1.1). The canonical-check CI gate has an awk parse to detect Cargo.lock drift, but the workflow never sees the local file. So drift is technically undetectable.

Two paths (decide which):

(a) **Commit rust/Cargo.lock to git.** Standard for binary crates (audit-harness IS a binary crate per [[package]] section). Trade-off: every dependency bump touches Cargo.lock, but reproducibility wins. The canonical-check awk parse becomes load-bearing.

(b) **Document the untracked status in RELEASING.md.** Add explicit step to the release flow: `cargo build` to regenerate Cargo.lock with the bumped version, manual verification. No CI guarantee but matches current behavior.

Per cargo docs, libraries (rlib/dylib) should gitignore Cargo.lock; binaries should commit it. audit-harness's rust/ wrapper is a binary that delegates to the scripts — so (a) is technically more correct.

Acceptance: decision recorded in a short ADR under 000-docs/ (or a CHANGELOG line if minor); either Cargo.lock is committed + canonical-check gate verified to catch drift via a deliberate test, OR RELEASING.md documents the manual step.
close_reason: Cargo.lock tracking decision made + documented (acting-CTO call per current Cargo guidance) (PR #69 merged 4c42f57e2d3e4449b01269e625ae713441e8db4a, 2026-06-18)
